reviews.title: Good insights
reviews.text: I’ve just been using this for a few weeks but I already see the benefit. I had an episode earlier this year that I am suspecting triggered POTS, although we are still trying to figure that out. It helps me see exactly how much energy I use doing different activities. I wouldn’t be able to capture this information without the visible band. I have been tracking my HR with my Apple Watch for years, but to be able to see that it take X amount of energy to wash the dishes, or work, or take a shower is invaluable in helping me feel more “okay” during the day with my symptoms. And it helps me feel like I have a little more control instead of struggling to do “normal” things.

reviews.title: Set up is horrific
reviews.text: I’m not sure who thought that it was a good idea to make the set up so complicated that it brings a person to tears this is outrageous we are sick we don’t need some complicated BS that we can’t even figure out and then be told by an AI chat that it would be at least 24 hours before anybody that’s a real person can help me that’s ridiculous

reviews.title: Helpful
reviews.text:
I love this app and all it does. Sometimes the way I feel and the stability score seem way off, but that’s rare. They ask for feedback and are constantly improving and adjusting things according to the feedback. 

There are things I haven’t had the chance to use yet.. like printing a report for drs. Adding where I’m using my pacepoints has been rough lately with so many things going on at the moment and I’m barely getting through the days. But even without that self-reporting I’m still gaining a lot of insight.

It really helps me realize that just even getting up to go to the bathroom uses a lot of energy. Showering and going to the grocery store or other event really add up. I helps me to plan ahead for special events so I won’t end up in a month-long crash. 

I totally recommend this to anyone with CFS/ME or similar illnesses.

reviews.title: Game changer!
reviews.text:
Shows what puts you in “exertion” in real time and alerts you (if you choose to be alerted) so you can avoid PENE/PEM. Tracks multiple systems. If you have an “invisible” illness, it’s nice to see the real time readings, clear as day.  NO! It’s not in my head! Doctors can see right off that you have a very real physical manifestation of your illness! And just maybe they’ll believe you…
Smooth app, not glitchy. Can be worn on wrist OR upper arm - comfortable. Quick to update daily notes. Clear, easy to use, good data. I’ve been using the app daily.  Love it.

reviews.title: Can’t BYOD
reviews.text: I’d love to be able to demo the app with my new apple watch which has continuous monitoring! Until then I’m not going to wear a second contraption. Let me know when this changes and if the system works I’ll throw money at you!

reviews.title: Thank you for reminding me
reviews.text: I’ve had the band for a little over a month now. I have Multiple Sclerosis. Honestly, this has helped me so much. I appreciate the reminders to rest once I’ve met a certain threshold. It gives hard data that demonstrates how much energy I’ve expended and what I have left for the day. It’s the spoon theory come to life. The company truly cares about their product and I appreciate the way they listen to feedback.

reviews.title: Got some control back!
reviews.text: I love this app! With all the updated features I’ve found this to be extremely helpful to my managing my energy. It has allowed me to see information that helped me identify what activities are causing me personally more energy drain than others. And now knowing where I’m at with my energy on a given day allows me to schedule things better accordingly. My crashes are much less and it has taught me not to be so hard on myself if I can’t get everything I want done on a given day and it’s ok to slow down!! It was really hard at first to make those changes but I can now see how much downtime I’ve avoided by pacing myself. This app keeps me on track. I highly recommend to anyone struggling with learning how to pace. It really has made a significant difference for me.

reviews.title: Invaluable App
reviews.text: Seeing where my energy is spent, how much is spent, and the warnings when I’ve been in the Exertion zone for a certain period of time have been invaluable. Plus knowing my PacePoints to finally have a number to know how much energy I can spend each day without potentially causing a flare is amazing. This is an amazing app for those with chronic, energy-limiting illnesses.

reviews.title: Apple health sync
reviews.text: Absolutely love my band and wear it religiously. I really appreciate the objective validation for how I’m “subjectively” feeling  it helps me listen to my body better and I have found occurrences of myself unnecessarily stressing/rushing through life happening soooo much less frequently. 4 stars because I wish it synced with my apple health so I didn’t have to wear multiple bands to track my sleep. Im curious why they chose not to give sync with health apps an option

reviews.title: Transformational
reviews.text: This thing has changed my whole outlook on pacing, while at the same time given me concrete numbers to point to when I have a flare. It’s brilliant & I’m still wrapping my mind around how transformational it is for those of us with invisible illness.

reviews.title: MUST Buy their wearable
reviews.text: Would have loved to try it. Already own wearables. I had such hope for this too.

reviews.title: Patients: this is a predatory app
reviews.text: I deleted my paid account,  this app is exploiting people with chronic illnesses. If you have POTS do not use this app. If you have MCAS absolutely do not use this app. If you have ME, this app can pose a danger to your health or any possibility of remission/recovery. Go buy a Garmin or an Apple Watch or a Myfit band, all will give you much better data and cost less. BEWARE OF PREDATORY APPS LIKE VISIBLE.

reviews.title: Started amazing - 2 months in inaccurate data - trying everything but replacing product.
reviews.text: I have loved this visible bracelet but it has had many glitches including the battery plunging. Talked with Nessie in customer service and have rebooted restarted reset let drain cut off - every single thing possible for the battery to work properly and inaccurate data. It’s like they do not want to admit this bracelet is faulty and lets drag it out in hopes she gives up. I need this bracelet to track my HR and when and why because I have POTS. This was supposed to show the Drs evidence of what is going on and when and why but here I am 5 days before my 2.5 hr drive apt and the band is once again not keeping an accurate HR so the pace points ate off as is everything else. But we are in the middle of another battery reset and watch by draining and timing to 10%. The bracelet has been amazing until things started acting up but it’s like they do not want to exchange. I am very frustrated at this point as this is not good customer service. If they replace my band things would be different. I don’t want a refund as I would like to continue in hopes maybe this is just a faulty one. We will see what happens. I gave 2 stars due to when working properly it’s great but when not working right it’s just another inaccurate fit-bit.

reviews.title: Misleading and Faulty
reviews.text: At the beginning of my Visible journey the band and app worked great. Six months in the first band broke the magnet for the charger popped out. Support was slow to respond but eventually sent a replacement. Two months later the band no longer connects to the app. Contacted support and was met with multiple rounds of AI bot responses. Currently going on 23 days without a resolution after contacting support. The Visible company products focus on the chronically ill and the disabled community. When Visible continues to ignore the customer’s concerns the customer becomes invisible. Dictating communication through an inaccessible platform the Visible app, the message becomes clear: Profits over functionality at the cost of the chronically ill/disabled customer. Still fighting for the $250 refund.

reviews.title: Good but expensive
reviews.text: I really like the app and my band, I find it very useful and have always gotten great customer support! But I struggle to consider it an “accessible product” due to its high price tag. Especially since it’s made specifically for the chronically ill/disabled community, a community that has more people who can’t work than can.

reviews.title: Soooo helpful
reviews.text: I find this device and app to be incredibly useful and helpful in regulating my ups and downs and overall health! I’ve had it for almost a year and can’t imagine life without it. It is very helpful in letting me know when I need to rest because of ME/CFS vs when I need to take POTS meds. It gives me real time data that allows me to make important decisions about my health. It’s kept my crashes to a minimum and has become a great tool in managing my health.

reviews.title: Need better reports
reviews.text:
I need better reports from the data being collected everyday. The only report offered in the app doesn’t tell me much. As a PCP, I would love to be able to recommend this to a patient who wanted to tract symptoms and severity over time so please add that if you can! 

However, Visible is great for pacing and knowing when I am in my exertion zone and need to rest for a bit which is very important to me as a person with POTS/dysautonomia. This is what keeps me as a subscriber with no plans to change!

reviews.title: Dysautonomia, long covid, HEDS
reviews.text: I now know when to ask for help and have physical data I can show doctors. Often, I feel I’m “making it up”. I know if I pushed myself, I’d feel terrible. However, I didn’t fully understand where that limit was. I’d just push and push…until I crashed. Now I have something that tells me what activities are more effort, when I should think about resting, and how my sleep was. As I go through, I’m leaving feedback for what could be helpful in the future! I don’t know if there’s an ECG feature, but I think that would be paramount to a lot of us. I’m in love the 24/7 heart rate because my Apple Watch could never! My heart rate is so finicking it was almost impossible to catch the right heart rate at the right time, with this I FINALLY CAN.

reviews.title: A wonderful tool
reviews.text: I had no idea just how bad my tachycardia was until I wore Visible. I understand now that I need help managing it. Now I know why I feel so very tired all the time.

reviews.title: Good App but Missing Value
reviews.text: I like the concept of tracking. I don’t understand why there are no iOS lock screen widgets and there is only one type and size home screen widget. There is no Apple Watch integration, nothing you can glance at your wrist to reassess your activity. The brand has grown from 1M to 10M revenue by $20 monthly subscriptions (again where is the value?) and still has not integrated sleep tracking, but it is in the works. I came back after two years to see if thing had gotten any better and while I do think it is a beneficial device and service, I believe a lower price point or more features being included would make this make more sense for me and many others. The company has a position for a director for 120-150k/year yet I’m still getting “start up” vibes from the app itself.

reviews.title: Needs additional features
reviews.text:
I would benefit greatly if the visible app worked with Apple health, Apple Watch (continuous alerts in exertion) and allows data export for my own analysis. I have to use the tachymon app with my Apple Watch to alert me when I’m overdoing it. I am a very active person and pacing is especially hard for me as I tend to push through the symptoms to complete a task. I would also like to see what activity tags are costing me the most points over time. 

I am very happy with comfort, pacing recommendations, tracking and battery life.

reviews.title: Makes Pacing Possible!
reviews.text: I have hyperadrenergic POTS, Long Covid and MCAS. For the last 6 years I have been existing from crash to crash, from one exercise plan to bedridden and back again. I’ve been told I need to pace myself better but was left to figure that out all on my own. As a newly diagnosed AuDHD, post menopausal mother of neurodivergent teens that clearly didn’t happen without support. Visible has become that support. I can see how I spend my energy, I can see why showers are so hard and finally I can see what things help me. So glad I’ve found Visible!

reviews.title: Would be 5 stars except for
reviews.text:
This would be a 5 star review except for the fact the symptom tracking only gives you four options. Basically everything is on a scale of one to four. As this is geared towards people in chronic illness/pain that is extremely limiting. I am at the point where on a traditional pain scale never at a zero or one, and I know enough about pain and limitations I will hardly ever say I am at a 10 and a 9 will be for when I need to go to the hospital. That really leaves 2-8 for my every day pain. Plenty of numbers to really be able to get detailed about where I am and try to track what gets me to that number. But with only four to choose from I will never be at a zero and I will leave the four for when I need to go to the hospital. Now I am left with basically a bad pain day or good pain day. A better night sleep or worse night sleep. They give you options where you can add symptoms and track them, but I never use that or the nightly check in because what is the point? When I contacted them they said it is to make it easier on the person who doesn’t feel well and I should use the word descriptions or numbers as ranges. So zero would be 0-2 and one would be 3-5 and two would be 6-8 and three would be 9-10. Anyone with a chronic illness/pain, especially a woman, will tell you they bring these graphs you can print from the app and you have many days throughout the month logged as zero the doctors will look at you like why are you here complaining? Look at all these zero pain days. I really felt dismissed and not listened to, like it really wasn’t that big of deal. 

What this does really well is track my level of activity and I can see how much longer it takes me to recover than I originally thought. After so many decades of dealing with this I would rest to a certain point and get back up and keep going. This showed me I actually need to rest twice as long as I think in order to be able not to crash. I had a day where I overdid it for too long and this showed that even when I was sleeping I wasn’t recovering. I have had less crashes, or really bad days, even while being in worse pain, while adjusting in the moment to my activity levels since I have started using the band. That is the only reason I continue to use it and not return it. I would love to be able to use all these features but until they expand their tracking numbering system it is a waste of my energy and time.

**updated**
After the developer responded I lowered my review to two stars. I have looked back and seen that many other reviewers want additional star system but they won’t do it. Every morning to take a reading I have to review my sleep. Good (I literally will only use this a couple times a year if I am lucky) and awful, which does get used a few times a month. That leaves me with fair or bad to use the vast majority of the time with not even one extra number to track if it is an average bad night for me, or slightly better or worse. And I have to pay $20 a month for something so lacking? No sir, too many dude bros who think they know everything.

reviews.title: Thank God, More please
reviews.text:
We need more visibility on long covid suffering and the millions who have been suffering from awful life altering chronic illnesses 
Make more visibles! And give us more options for further sophisticated information on our bodies and exerting.

reviews.title: Buggy. Only works sometimes
reviews.text: I have MS and was so hopeful this would help me pace my “spoons.” So all it does it keep track of when your heart rate changes and translates that into energy units you’ve used up to tell you how tired you should feel. I didn’t realize this was all it did when I bought the thing. It’s not really a super sensible thing given there are countless variables that affect fatigue, than just a changing heart rate. But I gave it a try anyway and it sucks. Days go by where it collects no data at all, and the battery only lasts a couple days at a time. I contacted support and they told me to update the app. The next two days after the update, it collected zero data. Then it died. How’d you run out of battery when you weren’t even doing anything?! They also told me to try to pull down-refresh on the days with no data. I did this and no data appeared. It’s really bulky and ugly and only goes on your wrist, not the arm like in the ads. Don’t waste your money.

reviews.title: Love love love
reviews.text: I recently got diagnosed with EDS and POTS, and I wanted to understand my health and symptom patterns better. I saw the visible ad on Instagram and at first was a little skeptical and nervous to get it. But it is definitely worth the money if you are looking for better understanding and pacing for your chronic illness!

reviews.title: Love this app
reviews.text: I got it a while ago but in the last few days I’ve been trying to take advantage of all its features and I think it’s helping me be more mindful of pacing and coming up with strategies to keep my heart rate lower when doing activities.

reviews.title: Extremely Helpful
reviews.text: I’m in the process of getting evaluated for SVT and POTS. This has helped me realize and be mindful of all the energy I’m spending so I know where I need to pull back a little. It’s also given me information to show ER staff when I’ve had to go to the ER and to show my primary care and cardiologist. I also really appreciate the reminder to sit and rest because I tend to pace and clean when I’m stressed and obviously that’s not a helpful quality when you have health issues, so when I get the reminder, I sit down and let my heart rate go back down. Honestly this band has everything from monitoring symptoms to monitoring heart rate and seeing pace points and what activities like showering take from your overall pacing. So glad I made the decision to buy this!

reviews.title: Battery drains after 24 hours
reviews.text:
I specifically got this tracker because it monitors my disorders and the battery life is a week. But if the battery only lasts a day, and never gets worn because it's on a charger instead, what am I paying for?

Also, leaving this review because there is no easy findable way to contact the company.

reviews.title: Pacing I can see
reviews.text: For over a decade, I have been struggling with balance. When I’m having a “good day” I want to do as much as possible to make up for the other days…knowing full well that I’ll end up sleeping for the next three days and still be exhausted for two more days after that. This helps me become aware and to limit how much I demand of my body. It alerts me to slow down and rest for a moment.  I’ve only had this for about two weeks, but I haven’t had a three day crash out since I put it on.  I still have slow days, but fewer and not fully laid out like a zombie on the couch.  Life-changing for me!

reviews.title: It helps
reviews.text: I didn’t have high expectations for this as I didn’t think my heartbeat would say much about my pain, but if I stay within my budget it is decreased significantly and I have actually accomplished more

reviews.title: Good but could add some things
reviews.text: It’s really good I just wish it would show me what my highest and lowest heart rate was for the day. And that it notified me when my heart rate got too low rather than just when it got too high.

reviews.title: Love Visible! Being patient with working out the kinks.
reviews.text:
I’m not a fan of trackers or watches as they usually stress me out. However, I love how visible has helped me to be able to alert me when I’m going over my exertions budget. I’ve been able to show my family what my body is going through and how it aligns with my symptoms so I won’t gas light myself. I know it is new and it will take a while to work out some kinks and add new features. I hadn’t had a true POTS episode since I started wearing the visible band but I realized after I had an episode at work that my band was at 4% even though I had it on the charger the night before so it missed my episode to capture my heart rate and pace points. I was really bummed because I never got a notification to let me know the batter level was low or I somehow missed it. I get notifications throughout the day that my band has been disconnected during times I really need it to track. I can’t get the band any tighter to make contact and my battery is at l almost full charge. Im also hoping we can get an actual screen/watch feature so it can be multi use and see our HR on the watch as well. I’m excited to see what the new overnight feature does! I have a lot of issues at night as well. I had to buy a Visible compatible silicon band due to the scratchiness of the original band. 
Thank you Visible members for making something that works for chronic illness and specifically POTS!

reviews.title: Great for pacing
reviews.text: I have had less crashing out since getting the band. I do wish there was more information/ podcasts on chronic pain. I have CRPS and there is a large community of us that could be helped if there was more available with the band. Maybe also having  pain scale in the morning and evening check-ins so that could be tracked without having to use several apps.

reviews.title: Life Saving - Literally
reviews.text:
Learning about this app and the program behind it changed the way the world looked for me in an instant. 

Having transparency in my pocket suddenly made LIFE accessible in a way I thought was lost. I forgot what everyday participation in society felt like, or what the world looked like outside my sickroom. But now, it’s just outside my front door again. 

Actually using the app legit saved my life, and reminded me that it was not only possible to learn how life could still be lived, but it gave me the chance to remember why it was worth living. 

As long as it’s still free and easy to access HR HRV & PacePoint detail at the 15 min incremental view, for the full user history, then I’ll still be an avid ambassador. As of now, my advocacy is even unpaid, because it’s THAT much of a good thing! 

If your heart feels funky sometimes, or if your vision ever gets dark on standing, you might want to consider getting this for yourself. Obviously if you’re like me and have ever been reduced to living life horizontally, you’re hopefully just waiting for yours to arrive. 

It genuinely gave me life back, and made safe, incrementally progressive recovery* an option.

(Recovery ≠ remission, but sometimes it can happen together. This is not a cure for your long term condition(s), but it’s a tool for working WITH natural capacity limits instead of against them for the purposes of regaining mobility. Your mileage may vary.)

reviews.title: Best symptom tracking app I’ve had
reviews.text: 10/10 app. Helps me as I struggle to get a diagnosis for my complex chronic illness and pacing. The people on the app and the podcast truly understand and it’s so nice to have a community that sees my pain and supports

reviews.title: Life changing
reviews.text: At 72, had MECFS for 33 years. I’m so glad I finally decided to try Visible band. Seeing actual data in so many areas helps me make informed decisions about “what can I do today?”  It has always been like shooting in the dark but I’ve only had this several weeks and am able to have better days now based on my readings. I feel like my data is very accurate and backed by scientific studies. Of course, wish I had tried it sooner!

reviews.title: Visible
reviews.text: It has been a dream when it comes to managing my CFS!

reviews.title: Finally something that can help me…
reviews.text: The data and trends I get from this wearable app is amazing and extremely helpful. I appreciate the research and dedication it clearly took to provide quality insights and metrics for our bodies. I have Long Covid, hEDS, and other limiting factors; this app has helped me greatly in planning how I’m apple to expend myself during the day.

reviews.title: building in time for checking in with myself with chronic illness
reviews.text:
I used the free version of this app for well over a year and then recently purchased the arm band/wrist band. I really appreciate the ability to customize symptom tracking while also logging impacts that may affect my symptoms, such as exertion or custom daily impacts. 

I have used multiple other trackers before, and even ones specific for chronic illness, but this one is my favorite. 

I will also say that the team does a great job soliciting feedback and making updates.

reviews.title: Love it more than I thought I would
reviews.text: I’m surprised by how helpful the data I’ve gathered with this is. It’s helped me pace myself and make good energy-use decisions. It’s a relief to have a tracker that tells me I should be resting rather than one that yells at me for not getting enough steps.

reviews.title: So helpful for PEM and POTS
reviews.text: I have tried so many fitness trackers to help heal—Visible is so far superior. Not being compared to a healthy population is a huge psychological benefit. Having a constant HR measurement is also fantastic. I’m able to use notifications to let me know when I’m exerting too much, and I’m able to avoid PEM so much better. It makes such a difference having an app built for chronic illness instead of making do with fitness apps. Battery life on the strap is also great.

reviews.title: great for SCI related injuries!
reviews.text:
I use this device and app 24/7.  I have a spinal cord injury with partial paralysis (and many complications).  This device is the OMLY tool to use to manage any type of long term recovery or serious chronic illness, including pain management.
It is a MUST HAVE -  I also own an Aura ring and Hume band.  They are NOT the same !

reviews.title: Shari Kimball, DNP
reviews.text: I have found Visible extremely helpful in navigating my own chronic illness. It is giving me valuable insights that have helped me better manage my energy. I will be recommending it to my patient’s managing chronic illness.

reviews.title: Great idea but inaccessible
reviews.text:
There are many with chronic illness that are low income or spend so much on health care, the cost of this apps monthly service plus the cost of the wearable really feels out of reach. 
The app itself is great, it’s been a fantastic tool to help with pacing and predicting what my day might look like, I just wish the app would talk to my Apple Watch so I wouldn’t have to buy the visible band, and that there was a discount for the monthly service for people who can’t afford another $15 a month service.

reviews.title: Pace points help me say no (and yes) without guilt
reviews.text:
One of the hardest things about chronic illness for me is the guilt. I feel guilty when I say no (to friends, family, even my dog when he wants to run around and play and I just can’t.) I also feel guilty about poor self-care when I say yes but I know I’ve already overdone it. Pace points help me quantify, externalize, and visualize amount of exertion in real time and shows me patterns. This helps me pace if I know I have something I want to say yes to later on, and it helps me set boundaries when I know I don’t have the capacity and need to say no to something. Additionally, the alerts when I enter “exertion” help me actively pace throughout the day and make better decisions so I don’t stay stuck in the crash cycle. 

I feel like I just wrote an ad for this app, but that’s how much it has helped me! So many other good things to say about it.

reviews.title: I am so much more comfortable with fewer hard crashes.
reviews.text:
This app has helped me to truly understand pacing. 

Before, I was in a constant state of crashes and I couldn’t seem to understand “why” and how to prevent them. 

I have learned what so called simple things were making me crash. Because of the level of my severity… I simply had no idea that feeding my cat or putting laundry in the machines were depleting my precious energy so much. 

Having this type of feedback allowed me to make appropriate changes that wouldn’t deplete my energy. A rolling stool In the kitchen. And having my washer raised. I never would have thought about doing this to keep me from crashing. 

I love having it remind me to rest when I don’t realize I’m over doing myself. 

Thank you for helping my level of severity be able to enjoy parts of life again. 
🩷🩷🩷🩷🩷

reviews.title: Game Changer
reviews.text: Kick started my recovery from Long Covid - ME/CFS with all of the guides and information on pacing. Made a massive difference in finally being able to get an accurate heart diagnosis for my tachycardia and get on the correct medication. Without a doubt, this app and arm band save lives.

reviews.title: Exhausted
reviews.text:
I would suggest anyone who has no idea why they are so sick and exhausted to get visible. I have been and still am tired but I’m learning how to pace myself. Before I had no idea why I was so tired or when I needed to stop and just breathe. I like that it tells you you’re going to have a bad day and maybe take it easy if possible. Those days I chill out now. Before I would try to get through it and then I would crash for days. I’m getting better at pacing myself but it takes time, especially if you’re like me and you don’t know when to stop. I think that was my biggest problem , not knowing when to just relax and pace myself . I’ve only been using it for a week and I’m already learning to take care of myself better so I don’t crash as much .   

Update, it stopped working and I have done everything they told me to do but just stops working only a few hours after linking it again and again. I’ve asked for customer service with no help. I asked for a replacement but I am being ignored , it only worked for 9 1/2 days  and they still charge me 19.99 a month even though I have asked them to cancel and give me a refund . I should have done more research . It’s a great concept but no customer service and it looks like they don’t care if the product works or not, just so they get their money .

reviews.title: Feeling Vindicated
reviews.text: It’s nice to see what you’ve been telling med professionals for YEARS! They can’t dismiss data.

reviews.title: Essential for managing a chronic condition
reviews.text: Visible has become a critical part of how I monitor my condition day to day. The HRV-guided breathing exercises help me actively calm my nervous system, and the real-time pacing alerts have taught me when to slow down before I overdo it — something I struggled with before. Being able to track symptoms and heart rate trends over weeks and months, then export a clean PDF summary for my doctor, has made my appointments far more productive. It’s rare to find a health app built this thoughtfully around actually living with a chronic illness rather than just logging data. Highly recommend to anyone managing a long-term condition.

reviews.title: Game changer..One of the only apps I consistently use - couple suggestions please to consider
reviews.text:
I cannot say enough about this app, truly the only way I get myself to consistently track my symptoms. The reminders help a lot. I never comment or leave reviews, only because I think this is so great. I have a few suggestions that I hope you could please take to the team to consider as I know you listen to us! 1) please can you up the word limit, we with chronic illness go through so much and I need some more space to write everything down. 2) can you have like a personal log system where we can write down all the acronyms we personally use for our own things and keep track of them. Like I want something to remember that SOB means shortness of breath, or what a “crash” means to me, things like that I can keep track so I don’t forget. 3) and most importantly, I would like to suggest a feature. Right now, for period it is checking off if you got it or now. I wonder if it would be possible to sync to our iPhone health app that way I can track period symptoms as well as ovulation. Since period does flare a lot of symptoms it is important to keep track but now I have to remember to log both apps since the health app tracks my period symptoms and flow. If this integration is not possible now I would like to also suggest a spot for better, more in depth period and ovulation symptom and flow tracking. Thanks for your 
consideration.

reviews.title: So much easier

I found myself struggling with whether or not my body was ready to try more, if I was just time to rest. My visible band helps me understand how my body is doing and whether or not it’s time to take that risk. It also helps me remember why I may be crashing a few days later than the day of exertion. reviews.text: This app has helped me have better stability managing fatigue. Got me off the cycle of overdoing when I feel well and then having a flare up from overdoing. I depend on the notifications to let me know when my body is under stress even if I don’t feel it right then. I know to back off, take a minute to rest, breathe or even stop my tasks completely for the day. I have more good days than before by getting info from my body I had no way of knowing before wearing this device.  Wouldn’t do without it now.

reviews.title: The band is 100% worth it.

reviews.title: The invisible is now visible!
reviews.text: So I have CFS as well as fibromyalgia and a few other things. I am 64 years old and trying to navigate these illnesses. I am learning to adjust my lifestyle to benefit My Health and for that I am eternally grateful. It is also beneficial to know what my morning stability is so that I can plan my day. I like filling out the morning and nightly check-in questions so that I can consciously think about how my body is reacting to my day or right after I get up from bed in the mornings. I would recommend this highly to anyone who has CFS/fibromyalgia/lupus/MS. Understanding our bodies and how they work is key to being successful with our health.!

reviews.title: Much needed
reviews.text:
I bought the wristband and started using the app after a lupus crash/flare-up sent me to bed for a week. Before visible, I had no visible way of knowing if my body was close to flaring up until I was bedridden. Now I can get an actual reading of my body’s stability first thing in the morning. It helps me plan my day. The wristband monitor tracks my energy exerted throughout the day so I can start to see what wears me down faster and what to pull back from. I believe it measure the time between the heartbeats, measuring for signs of emotional/mental distress, physical strain, and irregularities.  One time I was in a tense work meeting and the app accurately showed I was exerting an enormous amount of energy during that time. The next day my initial heart rate variable reading was very low. This told me I needed to make time for intentional self care before I spiral into a flare-up. This is exactly the type of app I was looking for. For me it is worth the money spent to prevent myself for more expenses like loss of job or medical bills when it could’ve been prevented beforehand. Good job, Visible Team.
On a side note, my sensitive skin doesn’t allow me to wear the device 24 hours a day so I wear it during waking hours. It still accomplishes what I need just fine.

reviews.title: Invaluable!
reviews.text:
I’ve only been using Visible for about a week, but honestly I’m already impressed by how much insight it’s giving me into my body.

I have EDS and POTS, and one of the hardest parts is figuring out where the line is between “doing normal life things” and “accidentally sending myself into a flare.” Before this, I knew I felt awful after certain activities, but I didn’t always understand why or how much different tasks were actually costing my body.

The continuous heart rate monitoring, morning HRV tracking, symptom logging, and PacePoints system are helping me connect patterns in a way I never could before. I can already see which activities are most taxing for me (lifting, yard work, prolonged standing, etc.) and it’s helping me pace more intentionally instead of constantly guessing.

What I appreciate most is that the app doesn’t make me feel lazy or dramatic. It gives objective data that validates what my body is experiencing and helps me make smarter decisions before I completely crash.

I also love how customizable and realistic it feels for real life. Being able to tag activities and compare them against symptoms over time makes it feel less like a generic fitness tracker and more like an actual chronic illness management tool.

For the first time in a long time, I feel like I’m learning how to work with my body instead of constantly fighting against it.

reviews.title: Compromised health? You need this!
reviews.text:
My health is greatly compromised, complicated and difficult to treat. My quality of life is poor and I’ll try anything that helps me live better. Visible is one of those things. 

I have Long Covid, a compromised immune system, spinal and nerve damage, constant pain, ME/CFS, PTSD, ADHD and a TBI. On any given day some or all can flare up and render me bedridden. I have a small energy window in which I can function. Visible helped me better understand and communicate my health and, over time, has helped me improve it. 

You won’t find a more responsive team or technology that is as continuously evolving. They are like us, with health conditions that need tending and that ordinary trackers can’t do much to help. 

I have been with Visible since the initial beta stage and have participated, as you will, in requesting features that help me live better. 

I easily customized Visible to track 37 symptoms and the 40+ treatments I use to manage them. I can identify how the type and nature of my activities (physical, mental, emotional or social) affect my health. More importantly, I can screen shot (or download) information to share with doctors or family so they know when I’m struggling. 

Visible evolved from just collecting information to also predicting how the things that I do (defined by me) will use up my limited energy. I make better decisions now and have fewer and milder crashes. It warns me when I’m using up too much energy and offers me a breathing exercise to calm my nervous system. 

It’s more than an app, it’s an ecosystem with community, research opportunities, content and support. There’s more functionality than you will probably use, but an uncluttered interface that you can take your time getting to know. 

May Visible be as good a companion on your health journey as it has been to me.

This has also equipped me with data to be able to advocate for myself in the medical system, which is quick to shuffle you around or be dismissive if your symptoms don’t fit a specific label or can’t be replicated at that specific moment. I’ve been recommending it to everyone I know, and I’m so grateful to the team at Visible for creating it!

reviews.title: Pacing is Life Changing!
reviews.text:
This band has been an absolute game changer for me. Coming to terms with needing to manage my activity has been quite the process, and I found it extremely difficult to really identify exactly what depletes me in the course of an otherwise mundane day as opposed to the obvious areas like going on long walks or being on my feet extensively. As someone with ADHD and some memory trouble, it was also increasingly difficult to track trends or similarities on my off days and during crashes as well. 

With the band, I’ve not only been able to track things that I didn’t think about (getting dressed skyrocketing my heart rate was surprising), but I’ve also been able to find some vindication with activities I expected but couldn’t explain (simply sitting in the heat is my worst nightmare). This has also allowed me to bring real data to my doctors to support my need for medical help and monitor changes in my lifestyle that make things easier in the long run. 

Ultimately, any issue I have with the band seems to be things that are not developed yet as this is a relatively new device, so I am greatly looking forward to what new resources arrive. 

Two things that I personally would like to see are a wider array of scaling options for static tracking (a 0-3 scale for social/emotional/physical is pretty limited), and options to add symptom types in the evening check in (fatigue, headaches, and lightheadedness are the main ones but there are plenty of other symptoms that may be worth tracking on an individualized basis).

reviews.title: Making my experience visible to others
reviews.text:
UPDATE: Visible changed their user interface recently, making the specific content I use no longer accessible to me. Many other app users have confirmed similar problems with accessibility in conversation and in chats during webinars. My rehab provider and myself have had extensive email conversations with Visible about this, and they are inflexible about refusing to restore the lost functionality. I presume this is because the app’s true purpose is to gather research data and not to actually care for the users’ needs nor to provide value for money. If you use Visible, I recommend using only the free version and considering it a donation of your time, energy and data. From what I’ve discovered as a paying customer, there is little to no value to the paid version of the app and the research data publications are drawing primarily from the freemium version of the app. It’s generous of them to make the freemium version so useful, it’s appalling that they upgraded the app usability and accessibility in ways that now exclude people with certain health effects from the very condition they are studying. Personally, this drastically drops the apps utility for me. Professionally, as a fellow researcher, I am concerned that these changes in the app design will bias their findings by changing the population that CAN use the app as well as altering how the app is used by those who continue with the app. 

ORIGINAL REVIEW: 
People see me when I’m well enough to be out and don’t realize what the rest of my life looks like. Visible makes it possible for me to show them how my pulse skyrockets when I’m standing, and pace points let’s me show how a bout of tachycardia at the end of the day can steal energy resources from the following day. Useful for documentation and communication.

reviews.title: Life changing and sustainable behavior modification

Visible and Copilot have become the most effective behavior‑shaping tools I’ve ever used. Visible gives me objective data about my energy, recovery, and stress levels, which has helped me finally understand why some days feel impossible and others feel manageable. Instead of guessing, I can see exactly when my system is unbalanced or when I need to slow down.

Copilot takes that information and helps me turn it into action. It guides me through pacing, planning, and decision‑making in a way that feels supportive instead of overwhelming. It helps me avoid the “push through it” cycle, recognize early warning signs, and build routines that protect my energy instead of draining it.

Since using them together, I’ve changed how I rest, how I plan my days, how I communicate my needs, and how I respond to stress. I’m more regulated, more self‑aware, and more consistent. For the first time, I feel like I’m working with my body instead of fighting against it.

reviews.text: Using this app has allowed me to make my extensive list of health conditions visible. I live as a 21 year old who “doesn’t look sick or in pain” but is constantly masking and “being ok” for others comfort. reviews.title: Review after 13 months testing to support Long COVID, POTS, CFS
reviews.text:
I went from a six-figure executive career to being unable to work after COVID. This is the first tool that helped me understand why and stop making myself worse.

December 2020, I caught COVID. Since then, I’ve been diagnosed with long covid, fibromyalgia, CFS, POTS, OI, chronic migraines, MCAS, chronic migraines, and more.

After years of being dismissed by specialists, a new doctor recommended Visible and said, “don’t get it for validation. Get it if you’re going to use it to manage your conditions.” I gave it a try, and it’s been life-changing.

I’ve had the Visible armband and membership for about 13 months now. It turned my invisible limits into measurable ones and helped me see the guardrails I needed to stop making myself worse.

I still have flares and PEM crashes, but now I understand the patterns behind them. I can see how activity, stress, poor sleep, and even something like using public transportation impacts my heart rate and overall stability. The daily stability score helps me decide what kind of day I am actually capable of having. So I’m no longer  guessing and paying for it later.

One example: I had no idea how much something as basic as showering was costing me. Seeing my heart rate spike, sometimes double, made it clear why everyday tasks were triggering symptoms. I can now also see how one outing can destabilize me for 1 to 3 days, sometimes longer.

It is definitely not the same as an Apple Watch. That pushed me toward fitness goals that made me sicker. Visible is built for people like me who need to preserve energy, not push past it.

I’ve also seen mental health benefits. The objective data helped me stop gaslighting myself and take my limits seriously without shame, guilt, masking, or minimizing.

There is a learning curve. It’s easy to over-focus on the data at first, and it requires consistency to be useful. While it will never replace my healthcare, it’s a priceless addition to my toolbox and well worth the investment. I offset the cost by switching all streaming services to basic plans.

If you are willing to actually use the data to guide your pacing, and you have an energy-limiting condition where exertion impacts your heart rate and stability, like I do, this can be a powerful tool for you, too.

reviews.text:
I purchased the Visible Band 2.0 and didn’t see any option during checkout to choose an arm band instead of the wrist band. I’ve since seen other users report the same thing. I never intended to wear a wrist band to begin with.I understand Visible can’t accept returns of worn straps for sanitary reasons, but the real issue is that I wasn’t given a choice of band types before purchase. I ended up paying for a wrist band I can’t comfortably use and had to buy an arm band separately.
I am genuinely excited to see whether this device can help me manage some ongoing health challenges, and the arm band is the only comfortable and realistic way for me to wear it consistently. I wish the strap options were clearly presented so customers can choose what they actually need.

reviews.title: Newly diagnosed

Pro’s of the app.
1. It sets a baseline for measuring relatively fast yet effective over a period of 4 days.
2. I’m able to add my symptoms not listed for personal tracking purposes.
3. Doesn’t ask for a lot of personal information 
4. Ability to upload after 1 month for physician appointments.
5. Helps with balance of energy vs time= fatigue + recovery time.
Con’s
1. Finding the correct placement of fingertip for readings. This could be case interference of my phone but it is a little finicky.
2. Best reading recommendation of morning reading is before you get out of bed.  Can’t really be done for me due to spouse so I have to leave the room.
3. Full version may be pricey though understandable under circumstances that it is a fairly new company.
Overall I’m finding the App benefits outweigh their negatives.
Will review again after by own Beta testing.

reviews.title: Almost perfect!! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
reviews.text:
I am in love with the Visible Band 2.0 and app that helps me track my heart rate 24/7 and gives me alerts when I’m over-exerting myself, monitors my HRV (time between heartbeats), I get to pick my symptoms and do nightly check-ins where I rate them, (and much more!). 

It then uses all this info for a morning check-in where it checks my heart rate and HRV when I wake up along with everything else to let me know what my morning stability is, gives me information on why, and tells me how I need to plan my day out. This is the most helpful feature to me and I don’t see myself going a day without it ever again! 

The second most helpful feature to me is the constant monitoring of my heartbeat, as I have a very high resting heart rate every since I have severe eclampsia in 2020, no doctor can figure out why or how to treat it. It spikes and dips, but any time I am up moving it likes to spike and my app immediately alerts me when I am over-exerting myself and that feature is so helpful to me because I know when I am over doing it and need to stop and rest. 

The app will slowly introduce you to the different working parts. YOU MUST BE PATIENT! I am not, so it was very hard for me because I was so excited. But trust the process, it does things a certain way for a reason. Make sure to get on the app daily! And when it starts to ask you to log your mornings and nights before your band comes, it is very important you do so, so it will have some of your information when your band arrives and it starts to do what it does. You will also have to be patient to get your morning stability readings, and other functions as well. It can be frustrating to wait, but it is important for the app to get to know you first. The waiting is worth it, I promise! Just make sure to follow the directions of the app! 

I left out one star because Visible is missing one huge component: blood pressure readings. I would LOVE to not have to pull out my clunky cuff and machine all through out the day, every single day. Most people have the feature on their watches these days, but I am not one of those people. I also do not like things attached to my limbs, I can handle the Visible band, but I cannot do anything more. But I truly would love to have blood pressure readings added to the band and the app with all the other information. I feel like this would take the Visible band to a whole different level, and I absolutely would be a customer for LIFE no questions asked. 

Please consider adding blood pressure readings to your bands and app! As a person whose blood pressure is never stable, and no doctor can figure out why, this would make a world of a difference for me in combination with my other information!

I’m not sure if this is a device or software issue, but I do find that I have chunks of days or half a day missing in the data when I’m pretty sure I was wearing it (it does not need to be charged often, maybe I let the battery get too low or I did take it off).

The main thing I would like is more flexibility and functionality in the software. I would love to, eg, be able to export all of the graphs for heart rate I’ve ever had. The data from the CSV export is very sparse and non-comprehensive. Even if the CSV could optionally include the raw data from measurements, that would be a basic improvement.

Overall I love Visible for the information but it suffers from mediocre software (like so many things these days). I work in software, and knowing nothing about your business… give your teams more time! More compensation! And realize that what they are doing is both difficult, and crucial to your business.

reviews.title: Beware of finicky tech
reviews.text: I want to give this five stars. The app and the data provided are really valuable. However the armbands are either profoundly finicky across the board or I have a particularly faulty one that they are refusing to replace. I have tried to be patient, I have done all the troubleshooting. But I routinely have gaps in data that mess up my pace points and the battery will stop charging and I have to go through the tedious process of resetting the devise. I’m trying to be patient with support, but I just keep getting troubleshooting lists and lack of empathy for how unbelievably draining this is for someone with an energy limiting illness that spent a lot of money on this. I’m not necessarily saying don’t get the armband because the data is so valuable when it DOES work, but definitely lower your expectations and be prepared for a drain on your energy resources if you do. It’s just so frustrating because we’re surrounded by snake oil and this company claims to be run by folks with this same illness, but this is how faulty technology is addressed.

reviews.title: Needs improvement
reviews.text:
For an app designed for people with chronic illness — and at a premium monthly price — Visible still needs significant improvement. There are several very VISIBLE bugs that the developers appear to tolerate rather than fix.

First, the app must remain running in the background to function. If it goes dormant (for example, when too many apps are open), it silently stops collecting data — and you’re not notified. That means you have to constantly babysit it. Once it becomes active again, any missed data is permanently lost because the Visible band has no onboard memory; all data is transmitted live.

Another ongoing issue is the need for frequent hard resets of the band. I’ve had to reset mine four times in just five months — in fact, I’m writing this review now because it just happened again. The band will suddenly stop collecting data, glitch out, and refuse to reconnect — even when the app is active. This issue is so common that there’s an entire tutorial video explaining how to reset it, which suggests it’s considered “normal,” when it really shouldn’t be.

On top of that, the app is a major battery drain when it’s running.

I genuinely love what the creators are trying to do, and this app HAS benefited me. But for $20 a month, I expect a smoother, more reliable experience — especially for users with chronic illness, where energy and cognitive load are limited resources. I was planning to cancel but accepted a discounted offer for three more months to give it another chance. Still, I truly hope these issues are addressed because this product has real potential — it just needs more refinement.

reviews.text: Yeah so I pretty classically overdo it and then I’m out of it for several days (or longer) and/or get a migraine so having something that scientifically says SLOW DOWN, YOU is super, super helpful. I don’t second-guess my Visible!!!

reviews.title: Background app refresh
reviews.text: Love the app and the insights from it. The only downside I’ve noticed is that the band doesn’t track anything unless the app is open all the time. Background app refresh would be really nice so I don’t have to keep the app open all the time and my phone battery doesn’t get drained so much.

reviews.title: Great pacing tool
reviews.text: I can already tell just from a few weeks that Visible will definitely help me better plan for my future. It’s amazing to finally see proof as someone living with multiple invisible illnesses.

reviews.title: Absolute Must Have
reviews.text: I suffer from multiple, chronic, invisible illnesses, and this band is helping me to budget my activities to allow me to still feel good at the end of the day. Or when I don’t feel good, I know why. I also now feel validated and seen. Having invisible illnesses means that you look perfectly fine when inside you’re unable to do anything because of the pain or fatigue or brain fog or exhaustion. The app, paired with the band, along with the videos, help explain that it’s not just physical exertion, but mental and social and emotional exertion. All contribute to how you feel and what you’re putting your body through.

reviews.title: Charging issues after less than three weeks of used
reviews.text:
I didn’t know what to make of visible until I tried.  It helps to understand better your energy thought out the day.
But  it is concerning that after less than three weeks it’s not charging and not matter the troubleshooting it’s not working properly. 
I wish they were honest about their product and tell you the issues. 
If you get one don’t take into the shower because it will stop working, I think it’s important to wear it in the shower that way you know how much energy that takes out of you.  Since it is an issue don’t wear it, also be aware that stops charging after two weeks 

I reach out to customer service but AI bot told me that it’s gonna take a day or so to talk to someone.  Once I hear back and fix my visible or replace it I will update my review.

reviews.title: Physical hardware won’t charge, expensive paperweight
reviews.text: I’ve never been able to charge the Visible band device, leaving it charging all day it stays at 5%. Without the device, the app is no better than a symptom tracker.

reviews.title: Worth it!!
reviews.text:
This has been incredible in tracking all of my symptoms and telling me where I am in the morning, and letting me know how much energy I have for the day. 

The only thing I don’t like is that it doesn’t capture actual heart rhythms and I need that for A-Fib. 

I also love that you don’t have to charge this Often every five days.

reviews.title: Extremely helpful!
reviews.text: This helps me immensely! I can track my symptoms & budget my energy for the day. I already own an Oura ring & Apple Watch - this is much more valuable to me at a tiny cost of the purchase price!

reviews.title: Long Covid/MECFS user
reviews.text: As a physician and sufferer of long covid/MECFS I’ve dealt with crashes almost daily for over a year. I’ve tried energy budgeting with a daily schedule, writing down activities, and scheduling breaks, but nothing has really worked until Visible. Having an objective way to pace myself has been life-changing and takes a huge cognitive load off of me. I am so glad this was offered as a resource  to me by healthcare workers at the Mayo Clinic.

reviews.title: Great help!
reviews.text: Better pacing than I was achieving on my own, even after 20 years of experience. Crashing less, being more productive and feeling less frustrated than with activity trackers that are constantly telling me to do things I’m unable to do.

reviews.title: Really Helpful!
reviews.text: This has already been incredibly helpful in tracking POTS symptoms and heart rate to be able to show my doctor. It’s helping to keep myself from over exerting too much, and even though sometimes once I’m in the exertion zone I really can’t stop what I’m doing and have to finish my chores for my animals or whatever activity or chore I’m working on, it helps me to remember to give myself time between the next thing I need to do and relax a bit. I’ve already had more than one moment where I’ve been exerting myself, received a notification from the app, and have stopped to sit or breath before the dizziness has started to kick in and I find that extremely helpful!

reviews.title: Great concept, very glitchy execution
reviews.text: I’ve had nothing but problems since I got my band, and it keeps getting worse and not better. I’m constantly having charging issues and support keeps providing temporary fixes that don’t work in the long run, so I’m messaging back and forth every few days with no real resolution. I really love the idea of it but with so many glitches it’s more frustrating than useful right now. I would recommend waiting to try until they get more problems ironed out with the v2 band and am considering returning it entirely. Really disappointed.

reviews.title: Helps immensely
reviews.text: Being able to see how activities impact me and being able to pace myself better based on that has already been helpful and I haven’t even had my band for two full weeks yet.

reviews.title: Concrete proof!
reviews.text:
Visible has helped me articulate my energy levels and how activities impact me to my friends and family!
I am able to show them that working for six hours took a certain amount of energy today. And since I know my limit, I am able to make a better decision about what tasks I do to finish out my day, while still making sure that I have enough energy to drive home and feed myself, etc…
Visible helps me identify patterns and make my chronic illness more predictable. Before, I felt like I had no idea of what was going on with my body. Now I have something to hold me accountable for going over my daily energy budget/PacePoints.
I can see the proof the next day, both in my body, but also in the data - my heart rate is abnormal, easy tasks take more energy, and I can physically acknowledge my fatigue. And so can my partner! He’s able to check in with me throughout the day and he’s learning how to manage this all with me.

reviews.title: Helpful.
reviews.text: I have long COVID and an autoimmune disorder. I’ve only had visible for two weeks but it’s helped me to know when I’m doing too much and which days I’m not doing as well according to my HRV.  I’m curious what I’ll learn as the weeks go by.

reviews.title: Wonderful product
reviews.text: My visible band has changed my life. With the visible band and app I can track my heart rate every minute of the day, divide out what tasks are associated with an unstable heart rate and receive literal notifications custom set by me to go off during specific heart rate zones so I know when I need to stop and sit down. Me and my doctors have so much more information to help manage my POTS thanks to the visible band. I couldn’t be more grateful to the creators.

reviews.title: Helps me pace
reviews.text: This app and the arm band have been very important in my process of slow improvement from untreated Lyme disease. It shows very clearly how crashes are associated with going beyond my limit, which helps me make healthier decisions during the day.

reviews.title: Good feedback to pace my day
reviews.text: The quantification of my energy level helps me know how to take care of myself for the day it also helps my family know when they see my scores. I have only been using it for a little over a week but it has been eye opening so far.

reviews.title: The app for those of us who need to conserve our energy
reviews.text: Those of us who crash and burn the day being more active than usual now have a way to manage our energy.  I used to crash and burn after spending a weekend gardening, prepping for family gatherings, or playing nonstop with my grandchildren, not realizing how and when I needed to slow down.  This app is helping to remind me when to take a break so that I don’t end up in bed for a day recovering from overspending my energy allotment.  I’m just at the beginning of this journey but I’m already seeing changes as to how I feel after a big weekend.

reviews.title: Help for tracking and predicting
reviews.text: This app Helps me track my conditions and predicts when I may have a crash or flare. Easy to use. Easy to personalize.  I currently just use the APP without the wearable due to finances - and it helps!

reviews.title: **Update!! So Helpful!
reviews.text:
**I was gifted the device and a year subscription! It has been amazing! Having a better understanding of what activities use more energy has been helpful. Also seeing how I can conserve energy in those activities. Seeing how I use more energy for the same tasks the later it gets in the day helps me plan my day better, allowing for more rest in the evenings. I love being able to see in real time what my heartrate is doing. This has been so helpful! 

I am really liking this app! I only have the free version and just having that has made a difference in how I am managing my day to day life. The morning stability score helps me know when I need to take things slower and be gentle with myself. It also helps my family know when they need to expect a little less from me and let my body rest. I hope at some point I can afford the device and the monthly subscription! I think it would be life changing! Thank you, Visible, for seeing us and creating something to make our life more manageable!

reviews.title: Very good pace monitor
reviews.text: I like the features available on this app- it essentially monitors your heart rate and helps you figure out how you should pace yourself to prevent crashes throughout the day. I gave it 4 stars because I’d like to see some enhanced functionality - for instance a real time symptom tracker (pick a symptom and rate it immediately instead of remembering at the end of the day). Also having some of the health related smart watch options added would be good, such as basic heart rhythm checks, pulse/ox and pedometer. Finally an interface on the band with the ability to interact with and enter basic data would make it a really robust tool to manage chronic illness.

reviews.title: This app has been a godsend!
reviews.text: I started with the free app out of curiosity. It was so useful that I upgraded to the full program, and it has helped my family and I immensely! I am getting better at pacing myself and not feeling guilty when I need to rest for a few minutes, and they are stepping up more when I need help. Having a printout that I can take to my doctor helps in that area as well!

reviews.title: Incredibly helpful
reviews.text: I’m so glad I found Visible. I have multiple chronic illnesses and this truly helps me manage them. I started off using the app for free for about 6 months before I decided on the armband. Listen.. if you can afford the armband and you’re interested- DO IT. It has made a big difference being able to see my body reacting to my activities in real time. It is teaching me how to slow down, pace myself and say no to things when I can clearly see I’m running out of energy. It’s also very helpful for symptom tracking and allows you to compare multiple symptoms against each other or against your PacePoints, sleep quality, HR, HRV and more. It helped me present my symptoms to my doctors. Absolutely love it.

reviews.title: It’s not all in my head!
reviews.text: After 25 years of hearing that, it is nice to have something that reassures me that I am actually right! Here’s the thing - we KNOW something is going on, but sometimes having some proof really helps us not feel like we are losing our minds. It’s not you - it’s your body. Pay attention to it. This visible band gives you the tools you need to become more aware of what preserves you and what drains you, allowing you to manage your day much more effectively. It also helps you to say, I’m done. Stop pushing through the pain because other people tell you they can. Take care of YOU. You deserve it.

reviews.title: The most helpful device
reviews.text: I’ve had long covid (and as a result several other chronic illnesses) since I got covid in nyc in March of 2020. Of all the trackers I’ve tried (Oura, Fitbit, diary entries) this has been the most effective in helping me manage my energy, track my symptoms and prevent flare ups. The ability to make tags for things that aggravate me (putting away dishes) so I can budget is so useful. It also helps to know there’s a community I can tap into for information and also moral support as this uprooted my entire life. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Best support I've gotten for my illness
reviews.text:
I've been dealing with Long Covid symptoms (and possibly some secondary conditions, still figuring that out) for almost two years now, and Visible has been the best thing I've found to support myself. I've been using the app for free to do morning check-ins and track my symptoms, and then for the holidays my family kindly bought me the wearable tracker and a subscription for the full version of the app. 

I'm still getting to know the subscription features, and I admit I was skeptical that the wearable would add much benefit, but even in the week-ish I've been using it I see a definite benefit from seeing clear, unambiguous data that shows where my energy is going each day.

reviews.title: Solid support
reviews.text: This simple app helps me see how important pacing is w an invisible illness. Sometimes my situation becomes invisible even to me. These simple numbers & inquiries keep me conscious of my body’s needs as I live my life. It’s like a gentle companion walking along side me confirming I really must pace myself. Thank you.

reviews.title: Valuable Tool... Even For Inflammatory Arthritis!
reviews.text:
TLDR: I can't imagine my days without Visible anymore. I wasn't sure if it would be helpful with my autoimmune diseases (arthritis categories) but 4+ months in, it's a game-changer. 

I have Ankylosing Spondylitis, Psoriatic Arthritis, Uveitis, and Psoriasis (phew!). I've been using Visible for about 4 months and it's helped massively for managing my energy daily and *trying* to avoid flares. Somehow the PacePoints are never wrong! It is also the best symptom tracker tool I have thus far, and gives me a tangible way to understand why I'm so fatigued (or sore) – especially when I don't realize how much energy an activity has taken. Having something that is proof that what I'm feeling ISN'T all in my head is validating and useful when it comes to recognizing symptoms. 

I'm an active AS-er (move it or fuse it!) and Visible has also helped me balance exercise with rest. 

Highly, highly encourage anyone with any autoimmune disease to try Visible.

reviews.title: Validated & Informed
reviews.text:
Visible allows me to understand what is happening inside my body, real time.  This not only helps me to adjust my day, but flush up and prioritize lifestyle changes and support tools for specific tasks I’ve been tracking.  Showers were my #1 drain and taking 3 days to recover my heart rate.  A shower chair has made a huge improvement not only to my day and week, but now I can take more frequent and longer showers. I would not have had this visibility without Visible. 

Lastly, I’ve been empowered to advocate for my needs, all data driven. My providers have been responsive.  I’m hopeful I’ll get a diagnosis & recovery plan quicker now.

reviews.title: Where my energy goes
reviews.text: The wristband and app have been so helpful for me to see what makes my heart rate increase in real time. The pace points is a really nice feature and has enhanced my pacing game.

reviews.title: Free version is good, subscription is excellent
reviews.text:
I’ve just gotten started with the free version of Visible. So far it’s been easy to use.(although I tend to forget the evening check in due to fatigue and brain fog) I’m hopeful that the app will make it easier to communicate with my medical team. I haven’t explored the wearable device yet as paying for a subscription isn’t within my budget.

Update 12/17/25:
I’ve been using the free version of Visible for several months and it has been helpful. The ability to add and edit trackers for meds, supplements and lifestyle then print /save a PDF to share with my doctor simplifies the process of figuring out what is helping and what’s not. I was still struggling to pace effectively though. I tried an app called stress watch but the delayed notifications weren’t very useful. Upgrading to Visible Band 2.0 and paid membership has been the right move for me. I really appreciate the realtime notifications when I’ve been in exertion mode for a while and the pace points budgeting/tracking feature is useful. It’s still early days but I’m optimistic that Visible Band + app + subscription will help my ADHD brain adapt to life with Long COVID.

reviews.title: Best tool
reviews.text: This is the best tool to pace yourself, to build up your stability, to prevent crashes and fainting. It helps you correlate activity with symptoms. I no longer crash for a week after high exertion tasks. I can avoid fainting episodes and monitor my heart rate.

reviews.title: Huge step forward
reviews.text: I finally have a way to track and quantify where my energy is going and help me prevent crashes.  I’ve tried tracking and managing it manually on my own and it was always too much work to maintain.  This offers a simple solution that is helping me learn where to hold back, allowing me to stay active longer.

reviews.title: Really great product for those with long COVID!
reviews.text: Visible has helped me to learn how to pace and allowed me to start feeling better. I had no idea how often I was in exertion just sitting at my desk. It’s allowed me to take more breaks at the right time and given me less crashes. I highly recommend this for those with long COVID or any illness with post exertional malaise.

reviews.title: A valuable tool to see how the body is responding to life
reviews.text:
As a person with invisible illnesses, being able to see the data supporting my experience has been validating and helps me communicate with my provider. 
My suggestions to improve the product would be to increase the number of symptoms that are monitored, a silicone band option, and to make the product pair to a different device process simpler. The initial set up was simple, but getting a new phone was challenging.

reviews.title: recommend for me/cfs
reviews.text: ive been using for a few weeks now, and it has helped me to start understanding crashes, energy and starting to learn to pace better. the data really helps, esp if you’re the kind of person who constantly doubts and questions yourself. with all the gaslighting surrounding invisible illnesses, making any part visible and able to clearly see trends really helps to be able to quiet some of my own self doubts.

reviews.title: Visible is So Helpful!!!
reviews.text: It helps me track my heart rate and helps me stay aware of how much energy I am using so I can make sure I don’t use more than I have.

reviews.title: Best App For Pacing
reviews.text: I can’t wait for new developments on this app! It’s easy to use and you get educated. I have combined this with genetic testing to help me hopefully get a diagnosis. I have been struggling with an undiagnosed autoimmune disease for my entire life and I think this just might help me finally get a diagnosis. I can’t afford the band and subscription but the free version is a great help!

reviews.title: Helpful but the arm band glitches a lot and wears fast.
reviews.text: The overall concept of the app is very helpful, and I think it tracks my pace points well. However, I have a lot of problems with the band. First, the most frustrating problem is it randomly disconnects from the app and I loose a whole day of data. Second, even though it’s supposed to be waterproof, whenever I wear it in the shower it stops working. Third, the band wears reallly fast, like I think it’s a bad material because I’ve only had it for a few months and it’s already falling apart.

reviews.title: Helps a lot
reviews.text: Great tool for managing limited energy. I have fibromyalgia, RA, multiple myeloma, asthma, CKD, and osteoarthritis. This has really helped remind me when to slow down. Much fewer crashes!

reviews.title: Would not recommend
reviews.text:
The band is expensive, single use. The membership process is glitchy. My account closed me out without notice or reason, it’s been taking days trying to figure it out. Wasted money and time. The program lacks guidance on when to schedule activities, just notifications to stop activities or “today is not a good day.”  Negative bias, this will keep us feeling and acting sicker longer, will not help towards recovery.

There are so many activity trackers that follow HRV and can really help with pacing and following your activities, and support recovery, not encourage continued sick-for-life attitude.

reviews.title: Visible Armband
reviews.text: In general, this app has been accessible and helpful. As someone who is visually impaired, I wish that they were full dark mode options and an ability to adjust size, because those two features not being in the app have made it very difficult for me to use over the past nine months or so since I’ve gotten the armband. Aside from that, I have loved being able to track my activity and gain a better understanding of my energy levels. I’ve had some issues with the band itself, but customer service has always been helpful and easy to talk to either through the app or their email support, though I will say that between an issue I had with the tracker itself not connecting to my device and then the band itself breaking recently, I’ve had months where I have not been able to use the tracker at all. It has been very frustrating because the subscription cost a lot of money and it’s for this reason that I don’t think I’ll be able to renew, simply between the cost of replacing the band and the cost of the subscription paired with the money I lost not being able to use it. I really wish the case was different because, again, I have really liked the insight into my health, but sadly I just can’t afford it.

reviews.title: Great tool for people who like data
reviews.text:
I am garbage about listening to my body and Visible helps me pay more attention to myself. It's frustrating at times and sometimes I get mad that I need to rest because who has time for that? But you have to make the time to pace and learn to let things go before they get taken from you. 

I'm still waiting for diagnosis but I suspect ME/CFS and POTS. I knew my heart beat fast and pounded sometimes but I didn't know how bad it actually was until I started wearing Visible.

Visible has helped me learn that my anger outbursts and mood swings aren't a personal failing of mine. They are another symptom of my exertion and exhaustion. When you're in fight or flight mode you don't have the energy to spare for emotional regulation. That's been incredibly validating and now it's something I can work on by learning what my worst triggers are, avoiding what I can, being more mindful when I start a task I know will be hard, and reminding me to take breaks and rest even when my frustrating body doesn't want to let me.

I bought the 2.0 band and was disappointed it didn't come with both straps. So I bought the arm strap separately. It's been hard to get the arm band to work. I'm plus size and squishy so it slips more than the wrist band and then I lose readings or I put it on too tight and the edges abrade my skin when I sleep. Having tattoos doesn't help! I have sleeves on both arms. I didn't see anything about visible not working well with tattoos before I bought it. It seems to read through some colors better than others. I have 2 pieces of bare skin where it fits but it's hard to keep it from shifting a bit when I move. I don't enjoy wearing anything on my wrist so not really being able to use the bicep band like I thought is a little disappointing. It would be nice if there was a third option where you could stick it wherever you want with a silicone dressing or something.

It would be nice if the charging cable was longer too. And if the app sent you an alert that it didn't detect a heartbeat for 5+ minutes. It's a little frustrating to lose chunks of data because it slipped and didn't record.
