The heart rate monitor is pretty spot on with its accuracy. I was hooked up yo to telemetry recently and Visible was never more than a couple of points away from the hospital's heart monitor. 

Overall though I like it, I'll recommend it, and I plan to keep using it daily.

reviews.title: Crash no more
reviews.text: I have had so many different trackers and they always focus on moving more, doing more, etc. and I end up in the same awful cycle of exhaustion. But this has truly changed the way I approach each day. I was very skeptical at first because see above. But my first week wearing it was thanksgiving week when I was hosting my family and I did find myself speaking up and making taking small breaks in between tasks a priority. I barely went over my pace points. I’ve also gotten very insightful data about what tasks are draining to my body and that was such an eye-opener! It’s teaching me to listen to my body again! Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Great way to count ‘Spoons’!!
reviews.text:
I am really loving how well the Visible tracker helps me learn how best to pace myself throughout the day. I have CRPS and I run out of ‘spoons’ very quickly. There are some activities it tracks as higher on my pacing that I didn’t realize how much they took out of me. It makes so much sense why I’m still hitting crashes. I also love that it’s waterproof as I’ve been curious to see how something like showering/bathing ranks on the pacing scale.
I’m really looking forward to some of the projected updates.  Especially if they are able to include sleep tracking data. I purchased Visible after seeing an ad from Chronically Jenni on Instagram. I did end up ordering the arm band after trying the wrist band for a few days. I wish there was an option to choose the arm band instead of automatically getting the wrist band when ordering. Or at least an option at ordering to pay to upgrade to an armband. Instead, I had to wait for my initial order to arrive, see that it was a wrist band, and then find the place in the app to order the armband. Especially since the ads that I’ve seen mostly show the arm band being worn.

reviews.title: Helps
reviews.text: It’s very interesting to see how certain activities really affect you. This band shows you a day by day comparison of what you go through in a way that’s very easy to see and show to others.

reviews.title: Visible
reviews.text: This band is a game changer. It has been showing me helpful insight and I realize that I push myself too far every day very early in the day and crash by midday all the time. It has allowed me to be more mindful of that and to try to navigate my day and my symptoms.

reviews.title: Helping me learn about my body
reviews.text: I bought this product because I saw it on Instagram and I was very frustrated with having dealt with chronic illness that leaves me completely incapacitated for two or three days at a time if I push myself too much. Of course the trick is knowing how much is too much right? It’s very easy for me to get started on a project or doing some tasks and then I start to get tired and I just keep going because I want to get it done. If I over extend myself then the following day, I can barely move or get out of the bed and this can drag on for two or three days. Having this product has shown me an easy way to see how much energy I’m expanding so I know when to slow down and I can budget myself better. I would recommend it for someone who struggles with a chronic illness like I do, or even for people who suffer with anxiety or depression that leaves them in a very depleted state after they have overextended themselves physically mentally or socially.

reviews.title: Helpful
reviews.text: I have fibromyalgia, this has been helpful so far. It’s helpful to track my heart rate to see if I’m over exerting myself at work. It’s nice to track my sleeping patterns.

reviews.title: Need to warn everyone about nickel in V2 band
reviews.text: I purchased the V2 band because I'm about to be traveling. There was nothing in the packaging that warned anything about nickel for people with allergies. I woke up this morning to a blistering weeping oozing rash on my arm because I have a nickel allergy. I am so horrified that this company is using such a cheap allergenic product for a population of people with autoimmune issues. I am utterly heartbroken and disappointed.

reviews.title: Visible making pacing manageable
reviews.text: This band and app have changed my life for the better. I am learning to better pace myself and care for my body. Having a invisible illness this is so helpful.

reviews.title: Garbage product
reviews.text: Band stopped paring with my phone. Followed their online instructions, deleted the app, reset my phone, all of it and it refuses to work. Their customer service is an endless AI generated nightmare and when you finally do get a real person, they don’t read anything you tell them and ask you to do exactly what you tried before being stuck in the worst customer service known to man. Waste of my money period. I’m now stuck with a broken useless waste of money and no resolution. Stay far away from this product and company, they prey on the chronically ill making promises and unable to deliver a simple Bluetooth connection.

reviews.title: Amazing for chronic illness
reviews.text: Love this app. I can see my energy levels throughout the day and know when I need to take a break. If I go over I know I’m gonna have a worse day the following day.

reviews.title: Fantastic wearable device!
reviews.text:
I got this on a whim from an Instagram ad, and I’m so glad I did! I’ve been using it for a few weeks and I’m finding it so helpful to track flareups and keep myself going at a steady pace. I didn’t realize how often I exert myself and it’s been such a huge benefit to keep track of symptoms and crashes. I have fibromyalgia, CFS/ME, and migraine and having actual data backing up how I feel inside is really empowering. Also, I think it’s beyond cool that we can participate in clinical trials and the data is used for research to help people just like us! I’m so happy I invested in Visible. If you’re on the fence, please take the plunge, future you will thank you! 
PS: Battery life is better than my Apple Watch, it’s very comfortable to wear and it recharges super quickly.

reviews.title: Life changing data collection
reviews.text: I have POTS, fibromyalgia, and chronic fatigue syndrome. I’ve tried to use so many other fitness trackers to collect data and manage my POTS, but it wasn’t the right algorithm and just made it look like I worked out a ton! Visible has the awareness of chronic illness factoring into HRV and heart rate   They are also working on new data collection for sleep!!! The app is super well designed and easy to use and navigate. The ability to track and compare data, both in the already available symptoms and ones you add yourself, is groundbreaking. This has become a resource I can use to improve my own life, and help communicate to people around me and doctors to give a more accurate picture of my day to day life being disabled. It has saved me from the self gaslighting and pushing through I still hard-headily do, even almost a decade into having POTS. Can’t argue with numbers directly showing what actively makes me struggle more! Every doctor I’ve checked in with since I found Visible I’ve told in hopes they will recommend it to other patients. Only ~$100 to get started and $20 for a monthly subscription afterwards, it’s so worth it. You can also access educational content from experts in the field and research projects being conducted across the United States!!!!! A feature I was impressed to see. For this app and to all the people who have and are working hard to create it, thank you. You’re undoing ableism within those who live with disability themselves and in everyone around them. This has created another level of self acceptance for me, even a whole decade into disability. Highly recommend and incredibly excited to see change and progress out of this development!!

reviews.title: Another tool in my symptom management tool bag
reviews.text: I like having a new way to look at my biometric data and correlate it to my day experience of living with an invisible chronic condition.   The monitor has no bells or whistles, and as such does is job well.  It simply collects and transmits data.  I look forward to the updates that will continue to be made in the app as that is where the insights are being identified in helping me more successfully manage my daily experiences of living with a chronic condition.

reviews.title: NV Beach lover
reviews.text: Heard about this app in an autoimmune support group. One of the hardest challenges about dealing with my fatigue that is often seen with my a few of my health conditions, is not knowing how what kind of day I will be facing every morning. And when I do have a “good” day, I often push it too far and am exhausted a few days following. This app helps me plan my day accordingly. I am learning a lot about pacing myself and making it a priority to not push myself to an extreme of then having to make up for it days after. So thankful for this app.

reviews.title: Wow, so helpful.
reviews.text: I love visible. It helps me provide data to my doctors, understand why I feel a certain way, and gives me back some of the control I lost over my wellness when I became sick.

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text: I’m finding it super helpful to see which activities are draining me the most.

reviews.title: Perfect for those with Fibromyalgia
reviews.text: I always wondered why my Oura ring and Apple Watch kept beeping at me and telling me that something was wrong with me but couldn't pinpoint what. Visible makes sense of my body‘s data and tells me how to pace myself and when to expect a crash so I can rest and prepare myself or prevent it from happening. I do wish that it came in a ring or a band that I could add to my watch because it’s hard to wear the band and a watch. And I do really like the simplicity of a ring because I don’t really like things around my wrist if I don’t have to. Other than that, I love the app and the level of tracking is on point.

reviews.title: Visible gives me hope
reviews.text: I've been suffering from long-haul COVID for three and a half years. Just went through a horrible crash. So I researched once again whether there was anything that could be done for long-haul sufferers. I'd been checking for years and didn't have much hope. This time I found Visible, and it's completely changed my relationship to my illness. I feel I understand it better and that I'm more in control. I adhere to my pace points as well as I can, and I feel like I'm making progress. Thank you, Visible.

reviews.title: Thankful and grateful
reviews.text: I struggle with recognizing my body's cue that I am over exerting myself and visible helps with that so much. I have POTS and this has been a game changer for me to be able to regulate myself and be active in my life! Highly recommend for anyone with auto immune, chronic illness or disease to be able to manage their energy AKA spoons!

reviews.title: Life changing
reviews.text: I’m still waiting for a diagnosis and this app has helped me so much to understand what is going on in my body so I can move forward with getting the medical help I need. The morning stability and pacing reminders have been super helpful to cope with an energy-limiting condition and the heart rate monitoring is the real time data I need. I feel seen and not so alone, and that is invaluable. I’m so glad I went with this app over the other fitness-oriented trackers on the market. Thank you Visible!!!

reviews.title: Real time help
reviews.text: This device is giving me the real time data to assist me with managing my Fibromyalgia.  This should help me to increase my productivity.  Increased strength and stamina.  It’s nice to have verification of bad days,  makes resting more meaningful.

reviews.title: Love it!!
reviews.text: I absolutely love this app so far! I’m currently working with the free version but it lets me see what my body status is for the day. Helps me realize when I need to slow down. Or if I do too much. My goal is to get the full version because I believe it will definitely help some with my hidden disability! Don’t hesitate. Just try it.

reviews.title: Worth EVERY PENNY!
reviews.text: The Visible armband has truly changed my life. The device itself is fantastic — comfortable, accurate, and reliable — but what really sets it apart is the app. It’s beyond anything I expected: so informative, beautifully designed, and genuinely educational. I’ve learned so much about my body and patterns just from using it. Honestly, the app alone is a 100 out of 10. Absolutely amazing experience overall.

reviews.title: Waste of money so far
reviews.text: It tells me when my heart rate exceeds 100 bpm.  A cheap used Gamin can do that.  Otherwise I see zero benefit and the mild harm of skin irritation.  It has one question for sleep quality.  My sleep quality cannot be summed up in in question.  Very disappointed.

reviews.title: Visible is amazing; I'm waiting to give 5 stars for reasons
reviews.text:
The whole concept is absolutely brilliant and desperately needed by everyone suffering from literally any kind of illness or energy/mobility issues. I'm just waiting for 2 things:

1. MAKE A SHARING OPTION FOR CARETAKERS/LOVED ONES. WE NEED HELP AND ARE SOMETIMES BAD AT IT OR LITERALLY INCAPABLE OF IT. 

2. Fix the activity tagging. It's not working - it randomly turns 1-hour activities into 25-hour activities and there's literally no way around it.

reviews.title: Mcas/pots/eds
reviews.text: I am trying the free version and it’s been very helpful.

reviews.title: I absolutely love it
reviews.text: It’s helped me see my physical energy levels and helped me pace myself

reviews.title: Can’t get app to work
reviews.text: So this platform looks amazing. I would love to use it. However, no matter what I have tried I can’t actually log into the app. If you can’t get into the app, you can’t use it and it doesn’t help you.

reviews.title: Lifeline
reviews.text: This app has been a lifeline for me. It helps me slow down on days I need to pace myself and sometimes I don’t realize it.

reviews.title: Visible with POTS
reviews.text: Honestly this app (even when I only had the free version) has helped me manage my POTS crashes so much! While the membership is really expensive, so I’m hoping I can keep it because having the pace alerts and points helps so much. Being able to track what activities impact me the most and see how much energy it takes really helps to manage the day to day even when you are overdoing it because ya know life doesn’t stop just because you have a chronic illness. This really is an amazing tool

reviews.title: Addisons Disease:Primary Adrenal Insufficiency:suspected Long Covid.
reviews.text:
This band:app:technology tool has helped me tremendously in aiding in better understanding &managing an extremely complex difficult life threatening invisible rare disease. Addisons Disease. Gaining insight of what is actually happening in my body by how certain physical,mental & emotional stressors can have major consequences on my body. Visibly seeing real time implications of my limited energy supply given towards every single thing I do is helping me to make better informed decisions,teaching me to Pace well as to where I need to conserve or spend my energy one day at a time, even throughout my day. This is adding to the much needed improvement of my quality of life. Helping me to chose wisely what I say yes to what I say no to. 
In gaining more insight in how my body is responding emotionally & physically at even given time as well as having morning stability scores has lessened the overall anxiety that comes along with the 24/7 task of navigating in properly managing of such a complex unpredictable chronic invisible illness in a healthy way by which there is simply no other means to gauge this by. Enabling me to have more frequent better days of actually being able to participate & engage in my life with less frequent bad days of being forced to stay in my bed. This real time data has given me such a tangible desperately needed hope I need on the very bad days Giving me more confidence in knowing when I heed to the recommendations given of resting along with pacing myself better I will soon get back up again! It is teaching me the critical importance of closely listening to my body’s needs, making those needs my top priority as well as pacing myself well allowing me to have way more good days with lessening my horrible full blown crash days. 
I am so very grateful for this tool! I highly appreciate it and recommend it for anyone fighting daily to have the best quality of life possible while managing a Chronic Disease. 
Blessings 
Amanda Sosebee

reviews.title: Managing symptoms and energy is so easy now
reviews.text: Where I used to have to keep a journal of issues for my doctor, I would always run out of patience. With this app, i can track each symptom I want to with a single click every evening. It takes almost zero energy and less than a minute. I’ve become more aware of my body since I started using Visible and I now understand when I’m overdoing it before I crash out. I know how little it takes for me to crash and what it looks like to recuperate without feeling selfish or down about it. I can hold better boundaries with family and friends now and honor my body’s ability to function. I can not recommend this app enough. As someone with chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, ibs, depression etc, it’s been a game changer.

reviews.title: Super impressed!
reviews.text: I knew I couldn’t have that strap on my arm but I JUMPED at the chance for the wrist band! I’ve had it for 5 or 6days now and I love it! I love that it tells me how many pace points (estimated) I have as soon as I get up. And it keeps track of how many pace points I use and even suggests that I should take a break if I’m over exerting myself. It’s a great little tool to have! And it’s pretty cool that you can participate in medical trials. The only down side I’ve found is how expensive it is. I wish the price could be lower so more people could afford it. 💛😁

reviews.title: Free app
reviews.text:
Minus a star only cuz of the price of the subscription 

I have POTS and HEDS and suspect mcas, tos, etc so i can’t work cuz of how intense it is. Which means I can’t pay for the subscription and don’t have the band so I thought the app would be useless for me but I tried it out anyways. While there’s not a whole lot from the free app there’s still enough to help. I get a rating in the morning from 1-5 telling me if I should pace today. 1 being stay in bed and 5 being have fun (still pace tho). I ended up with a kidney infection on day 3 of using the app and getting my 3 rating then my 1 rating helped tell my brain I wasn’t being over dramatic and I went into urgent care. The app didn’t tell me that 1 means go to urgent my symptoms did but the app helped me overcome the fear of going in by telling me my body is off balance and I’m not crazy. I really want to try the full version (it’s too spendy) or even possibly have some more added to the free. But at a baseline the free is still worth having the app if you struggle with slowing down.

reviews.title: Great medical assistant
reviews.text: This is a fantastic app and works even better with the sensor. The customer support is almost instantaneous, and if you’re concerned about that discomfort of the armband or the wrist, you can always tuck the sensor into a bra or even use a Band-Aid to tape it on. If you have an invisible illness, this is a great way to learn to pace yourself and understand how your body is responding.

reviews.title: An app lovingly crafted for illness sufferers of all stripes
reviews.text: Visible truly has been a lighthouse in a pretty stormy ocean for me! With PCOS, chronic pain, fibro, CFS, and god knows what else, being able to track so many data points and statistics with such specificity and accuracy across so many boards is just such a relief! Once I figure out how the sleep tracker works, it’s over for my demons fr 😤

reviews.title: Works well
reviews.text: The band works well, easy to wear and can be worn in the shower. I do like the notifications although I have had a couple of issues with the notification not coming when it happened but the next day when I’m over exerting. Also, notifications from days past keep popping up. Other than that I really like it. I’ve had fibromyalgia for over 25 years and it’s nice to have a useful tool.

reviews.title: Works well but
reviews.text: I wish there was a way to see where my pace points were without having to open the app every time if there was an Apple Watch integration that would be amazingI wish there was a way to see where my pace points were without having to open the app every time. If there was an Apple Watch integration, that would be amazing.

reviews.title: Pots
reviews.text: This has helped me keep track of my heart rate and my crashes. Love that it forces me to slow down because I overdo it constantly and then get upset when I don’t feel like a normal human the next day. Now I can see how things are affecting my heart rate and pace the day away

reviews.title: Invisible illness tracker
reviews.text: I have the Apple Watch, the aura ring but, they only track your heart rate every 5 minutes. The visible tracks your heart rate every minute. The only thing I would add is a blood pressure monitor. If have an invisible illness such as POTS, fibromyalgia, CF, and the list continues than you need the visible tracker.

reviews.title: Love this!!
reviews.text: I haven’t had visible very long so I’m pretty new to this app. I’ve tried other apps or wrist bands from other companies in the past but none of them helped. However, this visible app and band helps me A-LOT. I have POTS, it’s a new diagnosis for me and it has helped me how to pace myself.

reviews.title: Disappointment
reviews.text: The band does nothing my watch doesn’t do waste of money

reviews.title: I am learning to not fight my ME/CFS
reviews.text:
I love being shown when I get too active in a day so I avoid crashing. 
Checking in and being given a “forecast for my day helps me know when to take it easy and also notifications to stop and rest are invaluable. 
Also learning to breathe to reduce my heart rate is invaluable

reviews.title: Predictor of episodes of Long Covid
reviews.text: LC sìnce March 2020. This app predicts my next episode so I can adjust to minimize the severity. Excellent improvement toward a more normal life.

reviews.title: Love, love, love
reviews.text: I use this in conjunction with Rheumera, an app used by my Rheumatologists office. This has been really helpful for tracking symptoms and pacing. I use to help with SLE Lupus and Sjogrens. If you have any chronic conditions that can limit your energy and flare up, this can be really useful for tracking flare ups, heart rate, energy levels and fatigue. Easy to use. Easy to understand.

reviews.title: Easy to see trending readings
reviews.text: Glad to add it to my health tracking devices.

reviews.title: Long Covid PEM must have
reviews.text: Tracking pacing and activity is exhausting and often we are unaware how much contributes to our push crash cycles and how we can overdo. Visible app and wearable giving notifications to me has been hugely helpful. And the breathing is easy since integrated. I also love the activity tracking of HRV.

reviews.title: Great for Long COVID pacing
reviews.text: I really appreciate that the app itself is free, for those of us who have been disabled by Long COVID (2x, March 2020 & May 2022) to the point of not being able to have a job. I’ve struggled for years learn about pacing and to get a handle on POTS, PEM and my doctors often aren’t helpful. This is a really important reference for both me and them.

reviews.title: Amazing Device!
reviews.text:
I’ve had fibromyalgia, psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and Hashimoto’s since 2018. I also have PEM. One of my life’s biggest challenges has been figuring out what I can do on any given day. Like many others, I don’t like living without any clue as to whether I can go to do things with family and friends. I’ve been trying to pace myself energy using spoon theory as a way to communicate both to myself and others, but I haven’t had any way to effectively track how I am doing and how much energy different activities take.  That is until now! 

Now, I’m using Visible and wearing it 24/7.  There are 3 ranges - rest, activity, and exertion - and it aptly shows that exertion costs more energy.  It tracks my pulse constantly and, after the initial learning period, gives me feedback to alert me when I’m in the exertion zone, which means my pulse is high enough to reflect high energy usage.  Before Visible, I could only tell when my energy was seriously dropping without any early warning system. Now, with Visible, I’m able to know when my pulse starts getting into exertion territory and I can adjust if it’s possible and if it’s not, I at least know and set my expectations closer to reality. 

The battery lasts about 5 days and recharges really fast. That’s awesome! 

In case it isn’t clear, I am totally happy with Visible and I strongly encourage anyone with energy draining illnesses to get it. Don’t hesitate! Just do it!

reviews.title: Glitches make me not want to purchase the band/subscription
reviews.text:
I really like the concept of this app and the subscription/arm band. I have EDS and POTS and the morning check ins give me a lot of insight into my day. However, maybe 20% of the time the morning check-in shows an error message that asks me to “try again”, but no matter what I do it simply won’t work for the rest of the day, and sometimes multiple days in a row. 
It’s a little disappointing when this happens and there’s not any information about why that error is showing up and I can’t seem to troubleshoot it in any way. 
If this is an indicator of the quality of the product I’m not willing to pay that much money for a subscription :/.

This is the third day in a row that I can’t use it with no explanation, and it’s disappointing as this has become a routine for me in understanding what I can handle and plan to do each day. I would love a solution for this as I want to save up for the band, but i’m not willing to spend a lot of money if it’s not worth it.

reviews.title: Knowing is best
reviews.text: I have multiple sclerosis, and while I’ve had now 11 hospitalizations only since last year I needed to find something that tells me when I’m exhausted and when I should slow down, so far I really like it and enjoy that it’s also shower proof ! I do however notice charge may last 2-3 days and also you need your phone near you at all times or close by in order for your arm band to track but other than that I very much enjoy so far!!

reviews.title: Fantastic Insight Into My Body
reviews.text:
I’ve had ME/CFS for many years now, and when I first heard about the Visible app and armband I was skeptical that they could help me. I’ve never been good at keeping up with wearable health trackers, and I wasn’t sure what insights the app could offer me. I finally caved and got one after a friend with an energy limiting illness recommended it, and I am delighted to say that Visible is really and truly a game changer for me. It actually gives me real time insights into my body and energy usage, and it’s helped me avoid the worst of a couple crashes already! For that alone, Visible is absolutely worth it to me. 

Just a note for folks who want detailed multi-symptom tracking apps — Visible currently lets you track up to three main symptoms at once, which works pretty well for me. But if you want to track more symptoms, you may need a supplemental app or method alongside Visible. This isn’t a knock on Visible at all, just an FYI! 

So grateful to this team for making this game-changing product.

reviews.title: Spoons
reviews.text: I have been dealing with fatigue and crashes and POTS-like symptoms and kept running out of spoons every day. It can be difficult to know or keep track of when I am over exerting myself. The visible band tracks my heart rate and activity levels and whether sleep was good or not. I’m still new to it so I don’t even know all of the features it has but so far so good. It has already kept track of and alerted me to the times I have overexerted myself—reminding me to stop and rest. One feature I really like is tracking my heart rate during the day and tagging activities that coincide with the heart rate ranges during the day. Then it will let me know how many pace points (spoons) I have used for each activity. This way I can keep track of those activities that may be draining my energy too quickly. There are educational talks/videos that I am going through that have been so helpful. I do like that everyone here takes these conditions and symptoms seriously and seem to truly understand with an empathy that you can only find with people who live with these types of conditions.

reviews.title: Wonderful App
reviews.text: I’m currently using the free version of this app. However, I’m already starting to benefit from using this app. As someone with chronic migraines and fibromyalgia life is exhausting. Just knowing if I’m out of balance and need to take things easier has been a benefit.

reviews.title: Helps EDS and POTS
reviews.text: This has helped me so much. It helps me manage my energy levels every day and lets me know how much I can continue to push through daily life. I 100% recommend!!

reviews.title: Game Changer
reviews.text: I have CFS, Long Covid & POTS. I’ve been bedridden for 2 months; can’t sit or stand without HR rising 40-60 BPM. Have had POTS over the years but never this long. I knew about pacing & thought i had it figured out. SO WRONG! My daughter heart about Visible & my kids bought it for me. I was VERY leery about how effective it would be. I thought oh here i go - another waste of money. It is quite literally a game changer. I was overestimating (by 200%+) how much i could do. Visible is easy to use & has made all the difference in helping me pace. It gives me insight into my heart rate that was difficult to track. The armband is comfortable & amazingly efficient. I just ordered the wristband bc i’m overweight & it will be easier to wear than the armband on my large arms. I cannot emphasize how ESSENTIAL Visible is in helping me pace properly. Ingenious device.i can’t say enough about what a life changing tool it is. 💜

reviews.title: So far so good
reviews.text: Visible is really nice to have something physical to show how much energy each task takes. I have POTS and it’s very hard to manage pacing when society is very hustle dominated. Being able to slow down when I need to helps prevent worse symptoms. Of course there is no cure but every little thing helps. They are working really hard for feedback and improving the app. The sleep study has been a really good new feature that I’ve enjoyed.

reviews.title: Pacing for hEDS, POTS
reviews.text: Very helpful to understand my stress levels, energy levels. Good for constant heart rate tracking to catch the spikes.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: This amazing app has been so helpful with POTS/CFS. Pacing is one of the most difficult things to do and I usually end up in a yo-yo situation. The feedback from this app takes the focus off of how I’m feeling the more I use it and provides valuable feedback to help me pace my day. The free version is still helpful and I would have continued using that if it was the best option but I did end up purchasing the subscription and band as the free version was so helpful I knew I would benefit from having the rest of it too.

reviews.title: Validates my fatigue!
reviews.text:
I’ve been chronically ill since I was 6 years old due to Spina Bifida Myelomeningocele, a birth defect in which my spinal cord was partially outside my body. Now that I’m in my 60’s, I find I’m in pain and exhausted all the time but always felt like my family thinks I’m just being extra or lazy. Visible has shown me that I’m not crazy, extra or lazy. It has also provided me with information on actions contributing to my exhaustion that I had no idea would, such as playing card games or just visiting with family members, both while just sitting at the dining room table. 

I really appreciate the prompts and advice I receive from the app throughout the day and I am starting to learn how to actually pace myself.

reviews.title: OT using Visible
reviews.text:
I’m an OT and thoroughly understand pacing, but Visible takes it to another level. I’ve suffered from CFS and POTS 
for 20 years and was told there was nothing wrong. This device gives me real time data that allows me to pace my activities and slow down and rest when I’m over-exerting myself (rather than pushing through and crashing).

reviews.title: Accessibility for invisibility - help for POTS, hEDS, spinal cord injury
reviews.text: I have hEDS with POTS, MCAS, and spinal cord injuries due to cranial-cervical instability. This device, app, and service has been a game-changer for me in helping me understand and manage my symptoms. It helps me; it helps my PTs, doctors, therapist, family, friends, and caregivers understand and help me with a complex and pervasive invisible but very real genetic syndrome. On top of that, the device and service are impressively affordable, and the app is impressively well-functioning, intuitive, attractive, and accessible.

reviews.title: PEM is real. But I don’t want to get used to it.
reviews.text: I’ve been complaining about post-exertional malaise for years. I am luckier than most it seems. I sincerely hope that the visible team can find some hard data that scientists and doctors can look at and say “hey it’s real.”

reviews.title: Great idea in theory…
reviews.text: I was really excited about this but so far the app has been less than satisfactory. It’s constantly going blank and not loading, making it kinda pointless because I don’t feel confident it’s properly tracking my data 24/7..I have also had a couple crashes since wearing the device and although I have adjusted the settings to alert me as soon as I’m in my over exertion zone, it has not once alerted me. Really not understanding why I’m even wearing it anymore tbh..

reviews.title: Helpful health tool
reviews.text: Morning measurements help understand how to plan your day and your body’s needs. The texts when you have been in your active zone for 2 minutes or 4 minutes and need to rest is great! The end of the day check in helps recap your day and you can see how you matched your goals for the day. Great tool!

reviews.title: Life-changing
reviews.text: Cannot recommend more. This app and armband was so hopeful for my chronic illness.

reviews.title: Heart, cancer,EDS, & Autoimmune patient
reviews.text: I’m still fairly new to this, but it has definitely helped me see what is going on with my heart when I’m feeling run down and struggling. It helps to warn me when I need to take a break and rest. And, gives me something visible to show my drs.

reviews.title: Visible arm band
reviews.text: So far, I have had my armband for a little over a week and I am really enjoying getting to watch how many pace points I’m using throughout my day and I love the little alerts that I get telling me that I need to maybe slow down a little bit that I’m using too much energy. I believe that anybody with any sort of invisible illness whether it’s Hashimoto’s like me or someone with autism or ADD or ADHD or any sort of invisible illness would benefit from this arm band the only way that it can be improved by adding a step counter.

reviews.title: Helpful for Fibromyalgia, too
reviews.text:
I have been doing so much better pacing myself using the app and armband. It actually helps me be more productive because its real time tracking reminders gets me to take a break. 

Previously, I would just push through until a task was completed and it would wipe me out. Pacing myself has always been difficult for me and this system is making a huge difference for me.

reviews.title: For anyone who wants to be more gentle with themselves
reviews.text: I really appreciate this app because it encourages and validates the idea that pacing and rest and honoring “spoons” is important.  Even without the wearable it provides support and many of my clients benefit greatly. Thank you Visible!

reviews.title: More help than most medical professionals
reviews.text: For people with long Covid and MECFS, find incompetent medical care can be quite difficult. This app and arm band were developed by people living with these conditions. Their information is science based and up-to-date. The app helped me quite a lot when I was newly diagnosed and trying to understand the concept of pacing. You think you know what it means, but you don’t. Visible showed me I needed to slow down much more than I realized in order to get better from my post exertional malaise.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Incredibly helpful in monitoring. I can’t get the armband yet but still very helpful

reviews.title: Can’t track symptoms during the day
reviews.text: Can’t speak for the device yet as I only just ordered it. But the app doesn’t allow you to track symptoms during the day, only once, at night time check in. I feel this defeats the point, especially when you want to track the symptom of memory loss like I do. By night time I won’t remember what symptoms I’ve had throughout the day. I really hope that they change this in the future so that symptom tracking will be available at any time of day. Otherwise I’m not sure it will be worth the price.

reviews.title: A POTSie Perspective
reviews.text:
This story has been told before. A lot. But now I will tell it again. But different!

I’m a POTSie who also has fibro, a TBI, and mental illness. I got Visible to help me track my energy usage because I was crashing horrifically on a nearly daily basis. It took one day of usage after the ‘get to know you’ period to figure out a shower absolutely kills me and it SHOWS. It’s been an eye opener and had started to reduce my crashes. 

I would recommend that you ship the standard and large bands together - I’m a fat girly and need the larger band.

reviews.title: Long term user
reviews.text: I’ve been with Visible for almost 2 years. I think it has helped me with my pacing and I like that it alerts me to slow down when I’m over doing it. But, I am disappointed with the cost of the monthly subscription and the new 2.0 armband. I thought it was going to have better functions and more accurate reading, but the “more accurate reading” is just that it turns itself off automatically when you remove it, instead of manually powering off on the original band. I thought I would be able to set an automatic morning stability test, so I don’t have to raise my heart rate to get my phone and then lay back in bed for 5 minutes until it settles, but it’s just an automatic turn off time at night. I’m really bummed that after already paying hundreds in subscription fees, I finally upgraded to 2.0 for close to another hundred and all it does is have a longer battery life. I don’t think the price point of the subscription is worth what we get for it. And I’m feeling really disappointed that I upgraded my band for no reason, as it was easy to grab my old band and put it on every morning when I get my phone and go back to laying down.

reviews.title: This has become essential!
reviews.text: I absolutely love the visible band and app. Being able to track my energy levels in real time and pace myself has been so helpful in managing my crashes. It has also allowed me to share with loved ones exactly how much my illness is affecting daily life. The simple task of showering robs me of several points each time. That has been a huge shocker for my husband and has better helped him understand me.

reviews.title: Finally Something That Helps
reviews.text: I learned about Visible during an appointment at Stanford’s PACS (Post-Acute COVID Syndrome) Clinic, and I’m so grateful for the introduction. Visible has been one of the most helpful tools I have to manage my ME/CFS. The science behind Heart Rate Variably and crashes/post-exertional malaise is fascinating, and having something that helps me proactively minimize crashes (when possible, at least) is such a gift. I purchased the membership because I was so impressed, and I’m so happy I did. I highly recommend giving it a try!

reviews.title: A Game Changer
reviews.text: I bought the Visible armband almost a year ago when I noticed that I was developing more cardiac symptoms that i never had before . Fitness watches don’t track your heart rate 24/7 & that’s why Visible got my attention . Since a child I’ve had chronic health issues & it’s nice to see a product that is geared towards illness & NOT fitness ! I have chronic pain (muscle & joint), autoimmune diseases, fibromyalgia & neuropathic pain . Visible is such a great tool to help me track my symptoms & see how they correlate to how my heart is functioning . Visible has helped me keep track of data that I can show to a doctor & hopefully get more answers . Thank you for such a great product ! Finally something for the disabled/chronically ill community :)

reviews.title: Incredible
reviews.text:
This is the best purchase I’ve ever made. I love that the app tells me when I am exerting myself so I can decide if I can reduce my efforts or not. I went to Vegas for a work conference and no one even asked what the band was. I love that it’s a nondescript band that could be anything. 
If you have trouble getting it to connect once you remove it from the charger for the first time, just charge it longer. That fixed it for me and I haven’t had an issue since.

reviews.title: Surprised it works
reviews.text: It does what it says,but makes it sound like its doing more. Its a heartrate monitor with a app that really is the only stand out feature. The stuff for it makes it seem like its more like some of the top of the line fitness trackers that do heartrate and other things like temperature, movement, sleep… its not. Which is kind of a huge disappointment considering the lack of other factors in that oh so important “biofeedback” being put into play for your pace points. Once i found that out i honestly thought especially with how massively severe my pots is (sitting im usually at 130-150hr from laying at 98-100hr) this would be useless.but to my surprise, it didn’t matter. Turns out im still going to be exhausted… around a certain point… no matter what i do or don’t do. This helps me pace on those 150 sitting up days. And even know its a day for that extra unscheduled bag of fluids. I also have several other conditions and amazingly it does actually track their flares better than expected. Like i get spinal leaks i am currently in one that needs repair. My numbers show im not doing great and should rest more. So id like more insights from it. But it does actually work.

reviews.title: I don’t have a device-yet
reviews.text: While I don’t have a device yet, I’m already seeing the benefits of using the app after about a week. I can track and see how far in advance I might have a flare up if I don’t take it easy. I’ve even had enough warning to forfeit a gig work block for some rest, because it warned that I had a possible flare in the future, and a couple hours later (which would have been in the middle of my gig) a huge thunderstorm went through. I was aching, but I didn’t flare up! Because I started treating myself as if I was already in a flare up with lots of electrolytes and my heating pads. I am really looking forward to being able to get the device and upgrading my app!!

reviews.title: Not free and will charge $25/month
reviews.text: This app doesn’t show up in my subscriptions, says it’s free and has actually been charging me $25/month. When I go to cancel a bot tells me incorrect steps that lead me to a page that I’m supposed to be able to manage my subscription but there is no option to do so, only log out or delete which I later read will take the app off my phone but still charge. The app is alright, somewhat helpful but I’d expect it to synthesize info and track trends for the amount of data you’re asked to input. A waste of time imo and scammy that they charge when it says free in my purchase history plus no way to cancel!!

reviews.title: Will not stay paired to wrist band
reviews.text: In about 10 days my arm band has stayed paired for 2 days - I’ve done the steps to re-pair it so many times - today it was being difficult and after trying for 2 hours I’ve had it - I’m going to remove the app and get refunded for it and the useless arm band - don’t waste your money on this junk!

reviews.title: Doesn’t work
reviews.text: I got my band today and I was very excited to try it out to help me get a better ode on managing my chronic illness. Unfortunately it does not work right from the start I’ve followed all the steps o can find I used the YouTube video followed the step by step directions - asked the chatbot and nothing - as soon as I take it off the charger it immediately unpairs and turns off - I’ve run all the troubleshooting solutions

reviews.title: Helpful
reviews.text: It’s extremely helpful and I love the free version until I can afford to get the subscription.

reviews.title: It does the job - but that’s it.
reviews.text: My perception is that the app does the basics but doesn’t go above and beyond to make the right tools to truly understand the data. I’ve used this app for a couple years. And with all that data I still find it hard to understand what it’s telling me in the “trends” tab. You can compare but it doesn’t really offer me much value. And without value, is it worth continuing to pay the subscription? I assumed the subscription meant innovation and frequent updates with useful features but no. My perception which often is reality as a customer is that it’s another way to make money while providing as little return on investment as possible to the customer. It’s quite sad, especially that this app is designed for a community already suffering. Do good by the customer and provide an outstanding return on investment, not just the bare minimum.

reviews.title: promising but disappointing
reviews.text: I had really high hopes for this app. However, there are many issues preventing this app from being an excellent tool for people with chronic conditions. Unfortunately, the app starts to assume that if you have a long period of flare or other concerning episodes associated with your condition, then it starts to reset your normal and you’re unable to use the stability score system. Also just be aware that if you have Raynaud’s phenomenon, then this will likely not work for you because your hands have to be warm for the sensor to catch your HRV. The customization for tracking your assistance is great, but you can Input this without getting an HRV reading. So you can’t just use this app as a symptom tracker.

reviews.title: Superb. Precise. Life changing.
reviews.text: I’ve been searching for a digital partner for years to help me navigate me/cfs and support my capacity to better understand and improve my debilitating symptoms. No other app or tracking tool I tried was remotely elegant or powerful. Then I found Visible. In just a few short weeks using the app and arm band I’m radically improving my awareness and capacity to track activities, investigate causes of PEM, and generally understand the fundamentals of my body and this complex condition. The UI, also, is phenomenal. The video and podcast resources are insightful. And the pacing system is genius. Bravo to the team! Worth every cent.

reviews.title: Band won’t work if it isn’t on the charger. Poor customer support.
reviews.text: Needs a lot more development. I have been trying for two days to get the band to function. I have sent several messages to their support and have no response. This is stress I didn’t need added. I was so excited to have some tool to track what activities make my heart rate act out and know when I was over doing it. Now I’m just frustrated and have wasted money.

reviews.title: Thankful for products like these
reviews.text:
I don’t have long covid but I have several chronic illnesses that operate very similarly. The ability to see my pacing in real
time to prevent further crashes has been invaluable. The only reason I do not give it 5 stars is that I wish there was a way to wear the monitor somewhere other than the upper arm (maybe the wrist?). Not only for the visibility of it but for more comfort—I find having constricting things on my arms to be very uncomfortable which leads me to not want to wear it all the time, but I do anyway bc I want the data!

reviews.title: heart disease managed
reviews.text: i was diagnosed in April with heart disease and manage chronic chest pain and crashes. not only does visible monitor my heart rate and i can input my symptoms it taught me how to pace myself day to day to avoid hard crashes. i highly recommend even if you have a disability that’s not listed as one of the main ones :)

reviews.title: Free version is amazing
reviews.text: Haven’t tried the membership but the free version is amazing and has improved my life.

reviews.title: The company does not support the monitor
reviews.text: The polar monitoring device was defective from the first time I tried to pair it to my phone. Customer support kept suggesting more fixes that DID NOT WORK. After 30 days I only got 5 days of valid monitoring, a clearly defective device they charged me for the next month’s monitoring for a defective device. They are not responding to my complaint and request for a new device or full refund. Furthermore the stress of dealing with this non responsive company has put me in a flare.

reviews.title: Best Tool I Have Tried
reviews.text: I have had long Covid for three years.  Many medical specialists have recommended pacing.  I tried other apps, but heart rate notifications not come in a timely enough way to be practical help.  This app not only gives near instantaneous heart rate notifications, but also allows you to track symptoms and associate them with your activities.  It was not until I could do all of this in one app that I was able to find practical energy-wasting trends.  I highly recommend the Visible app.

reviews.title: Chronically overdoing
reviews.text: I have a history of not listening to my body. I refused for so long to realize how much my chronic illness had progressed. My sister got visible a couple months ago and noticed a difference. She got it for me to track my heart rate and energy exertion. It has helped bring to reality the changes my body has made. Thank you

reviews.title: Really helpful
reviews.text: I appreciate this alerts me when I’m overdoing it and gives me the chance to pace better. It’s also a great way to check in with myself and document items to review with my Drs. Would be amazing as a watch app to keep the connection when away from the phone:)

reviews.title: Truly helps pace limited energy
reviews.text:
Over the past few years I’ve been struggling more and more with energy levels that are not obvious enough to yet receive a diagnosis. Most days I struggle to do the bare minimum to care for myself or tidy up. Random days I’ll sleep well, have a lot of energy and get a lot done, but then days later I’ll be exhausted. I was tired of not knowing why and not knowing how to pace myself. I had gone to my cardiologist and to another doctor who ran tests and said I seem relatively healthy. 

I saw Visible advertised several times on Instagram, but didn’t think initially that it applied to me. Over time I realized I needed SOMETHING to help me collect energy data, not just activity data on my smart watch. I needed to see what’s going on in my body, and I needed help with pacing. I needed to see if there were any trends I had so I could see what helped and what hurt my energy levels. 

I’ve now had visible for 2 weeks, and I’m so grateful for the data it’s been collecting. The morning stability score has been on the nose and the pace points help me to not overexert myself. Being able to see my heart rate variable, and to get warnings so that I slow down, or at least so I’m alert why I’ll be tired and need to rest later if I cannot stop a task, is helping both myself and my partner tremendously. I’m finding I’m actually able to accomplish more and communicate my needs better because I now see when I need to rest and when I have more energy to get things done.

reviews.title: LOVE IT
reviews.text: Absolutely amazing! I’ve had mine for about 2 weeks and it’s causing a huge difference in my days and generally helping me get back to living a normal life since pots has taken so much from me. Truly love this product!

reviews.title: It’s so validating
reviews.text: While the free app is helpful, I’d still get the visible band for all its features. You can check your morning stability with your phone camera, and get your score, to determine your day. I have POTS, IST, and other autoimmune issues, and with the app, alongside with the band, it has helped me to see (and show others) when I’m struggling with my day. You see your spikes for things you wouldn’t think twice about, like a shower or doing your hair. And you see how much energy you used up doing it, so you can recalculate the rest of your day. There are podcasts and lessons available as well, and you can even sign up for medical research from the app.

reviews.title: Goes the extra mile no other band does.
reviews.text: Being able to look at the nitty gritty and figure out easier what causes my exertion zones; has helped me in such significant ways. This band has really changed my life, I’ve got a number of disabilities that this little piece of tech helps. It really is just the small things, that make a huge impact.

reviews.title: Best $ I’ve Ever Spent
reviews.text: Had monitor for about a week and it’s already earned its keep. It tracks my energy expenditure and warns me when over-expending so I can rest. It’s been very accurate and has improved my QOL.

reviews.title: Would be more beneficial if I could afford the armband and subscription
reviews.text: I’ve only been using the app for a week but it very helpful to see how I am feeling affirmed by the HRV. However I can inly work part time because of my health and can in no way afford the subscription nor the armband—which I couldn’t wear consistently because HR detection devices cause deep pain after a few day. It would be more helpful if I could at least utilize the phone camera to take periodic readings.

reviews.title: Helps me to be softer to myself on tough days
reviews.text: Visible is helping me to see myself with more kindness and grace. On the tough days, it helps me to remember to be soft and take better care of myself. I love how I can track my symptoms. Recommend it 100%. Living with an invisible illness, I can forget to listen to what my body needs and ignore the urge to slow down in times that I feel a little better. This app helps me remember to pace myself and not over do it and crash.

reviews.title: Life-Changing
reviews.text: I’ve been dealing with sudden health issues for over a year that doctors haven’t been able to figure out. Before Visible I struggled keeping track of symptom highs and lows and changing energy levels - one day I’d barely be able to do anything and be so fatigued I could barely leave my bed, then the next I’d have energy and be more productive. With Visible I’m able to see if there are patterns in my symptoms and can see predictions in my energy for the day. It’s been a real life-changer

reviews.title: Great app free with out the arm band.
reviews.text: Love this app wish it was also free if you bought the arm band I do hear that they’re trying to make it to where insurance will pay for the arm band and the app so hope that comes through but otherwise the free version is great. Love it for tracking all of my illnesses and my fatigue.

reviews.title: Thrilled!
reviews.text: I’m not sure what I exactly hoped for when I decided to try Visible, but I didn’t expect it to be such a profound addition to my day to day living with chronic illness. I feel a sense of control and agency I haven’t felt in a long time, being able to objectively track my energy expenditures and other factors and make decisions accordingly. I am finally not having to retrofit a “fitness” device to meet my illness and feeling lousier about all the things I’m not doing or can’t do. This is the tool I’ve been wanting for years! I also LOVE being able to participate in research so seamlessly via Visible.

reviews.title: Doesn’t take into account people with severe illness
reviews.text:
I like the idea of this but currently it’s set up by and for people who are comparatively healthier, and clearly was not developed in consultation with people dealing with severe and very severe forms of the diseases in question. I urge Visible to convene a (paid) group of more severely affected users empowered to direct product development on the many changes needed to decrease how taxing the app is to use. This would also improve the experience of people who are well enough to use Visible as is, but would be better off if they didn’t have to use so many spoons (after all the point of the app). This is the benefit of universal design.

ETA: as this advice goes ignore, and the app continues to be way too complex to use, I have lowered my rating to one star. This causes me more harm than it helps.

reviews.title: Essential
reviews.text: This is an essential piece of equipment that I didn’t realize was essential until I got it. If you suffer from chronic fatigue, you won’t regret this purchase.

reviews.title: Visible is my go-to app for tracking, pacing, and improving my health with confidence
reviews.text: Visible has transformed how I manage my health. HR monitoring, symptom tracking, and pacing tools help me avoid crashes and make better choices. Relaxation tools and HRV tracking support recovery, while the symptom data empowers me and my care team to make informed decisions. A must-have for anyone wanting to improve function and well-being.

reviews.title: I love it
reviews.text: This app has helped me so much!

reviews.title: Finally I can make plans!
reviews.text:
This device has given me control back of my life. I have psoriatic arthritis and this can tell me when to take it easy and when I can push. It’s so nice to live my life and not crash out unexpectedly. 

More devices should focus on not just pushing through for fitness but for preserving your physical and mental health. 

I would like more band options though. Other than that it’s great!

reviews.title: Validation!
reviews.text: I’ve been using the free version and it’s so helpful to see how my body is really doing so I can adjust my day and not get worse. It’s also helpful to keep track of symptoms and see patterns. Love it so far.

reviews.title: I wish I had gotten it sooner
reviews.text: This device is so helpful and insightful. Getting a morning report to plan my day around is incredibly stress relieving as I know which days to stay home.

reviews.title: Love love love!!!
reviews.text: The armband and app have literally changed my life. I’ve been able to get through to doctors who in the past wouldn’t listen and budget my day so I don’t crash as often!

reviews.title: Worth it!
reviews.text: I have me/cfs, the tracking and heart rate notifications are really helpful for me so I know when I’m over exerting myself. It was pricey to get started with the wristband and the subscription, but for me it was definitely worth it.

reviews.title: Exceptional
reviews.text: I have ME/CFS & cannot believe how helpful this arm band has been. Worth every penny in my mind for the analysts alone.

reviews.title: Needs a few bugs fixed
reviews.text: I absolutely love this app and the whole concept of it- only thing is I feel like they should give you two armbands (just the band) when you first subscribe because the first arm band is gonna get gross after you wear it for a long time. It also has a few bugs. On certain days It won’t let me record my measurements because it says I am moving too much yet I am sitting still each time. I even do it with the camera monitor part but it also wouldn’t let me do it. For one day I couldn’t connect to my band for a while once I had something else connected to my Bluetooth, which is something that’s a little frustrating, cause I wasn’t able to use it for a full day. But otherwise, I absolutely love this. It is a great device. It’s been so helpful to track my POTS and pace myself.

reviews.title: Life Changing
reviews.text:
Essential for anyone who has primary fatigue. Being able to visualize when you are in “activity” even when you may consider yourself at rest is the to only thing that makes pacing work. Also seeing how sleep and infection affect your baseline is important. None of that was possible before.
I also really appreciate the level of support and responsiveness, though I know it may not continue into the future.

reviews.title: A must-have
reviews.text:
I held off on trying Visible for a bit, and my only regret is that I didn’t sign up for it immediately. Other wearables (I’ve tried Apple Watch and the Oura ring) don’t hold a candle to this for learning how my energy-limiting illness functions in real time and managing it. The team’s expertise and focus on us and our unique needs is so clear in the app’s design.

I’m wary of subscriptions in general, but this is worth every penny, and I dearly want it to continue and expand its availability all over the world. Everyone with this kind of condition needs Visible.

reviews.title: Chronic fatigue syndrome
reviews.text: I struggle with counting my spoons each day and often caused myself more harm by overdoing. This has taken the guess work out and also teaches me to tune in to how my body feels during each varied vital state. If I ignore it I have a harder time later so it’s pretty accurate. I can’t wait to get the arm band for better understanding of my body’s needs and for contributing to the research.

reviews.title: It’s ok
reviews.text: If you have the armband, the heart rate graph with times of day is great but I feel like the “alerts” are marketed a bit deceivingly. It only alerts you on your phone and the pacer is not very helpful. It would be way better if it also alerted you when your heart rate is going too high. It would be great if the actual armband vibrated to alert you too.

reviews.title: Love!
reviews.text:
Love the fact that this app gives you back control of your life. Gaining a sense of what triggers flare ups is a huge game changer in quality of life for me. 

The team is also very responsive and updates the app based on users—which is a huge bonus! You can tell the team cares about its customers. 

I also love the guidance they offer. There’s different lessons and strategies for anything you can imagine, and if you have a question that isn’t answered in the app, the team is willing to help.

reviews.title: Visible is helpful
reviews.text: This app is helping me to pay attention to my body and its ability / inability to function well

reviews.title: Great - one feature request
reviews.text:
So far, I’m very pleased. The two check-in types are thoughtfully implemented and easy to finish. My goal for usage is more for the symptom tracking over energy management. My symptoms are varied, complex, cyclical, and … well … frustrating. I hope to use this tracking to assist the specialists I’m seeing with better understanding and managing my situation. 

There’s one feature, though, that I’d love to see added. For nerve pain, for example, the ability to mark or otherwise specify where the pain is each day would be a big improvement. My nerve pain is random each day it occurs, and it would help in talking with my neurologist. I’m sure those with muscle and joint pain might benefit as well. I can add a note, but some other apps track it along with the pain rating. Just a thought/request. 

(As a developer myself, I know this would introduce a new one-to-many dataset to track and present. So I realize it’s not a simple change.)

Thanks so much for making this app free!

reviews.title: Great app and device
reviews.text: I got the visible armband to help me pace after developing Long Covid and a heart condition. The app is super sleek and well thought out, and it provides great information to track your heart rate and exertion. I highly recommend it for chronically ill folks.

reviews.title: Evening Check-Ins: Noticing My Self-Accommodations (and it is free!)
reviews.text: After a life of not accepting where I make accommodations for myself and my limitations, I now get to go through a check list each evening (with the ability to add and remove items as needed—including custom items). I have begun to notice signs of fatigue before burn out, and I am only utilizing the free potion of the app!

reviews.title: Gives me hope
reviews.text: I love my armband. I wear it 24/7. My illness is MECFS & I’m able to see my improvements by using Visible even though it’s a very slow process. Thank you guys for doing what you do!!

reviews.title: Life-Changing
reviews.text: The app and band have completely changed my life. They’ve helped me pace myself, see actual concrete data about my illnesses, and understand triggers. Because of Visible, I have been able to give my support network and doctors quantitative data. Because of this data, I finally received a POTS diagnosis and testing that led to the diagnosis of a serious heart condition. The customer support has been incredible, and in my opinion the pricing is very reasonable (as of 2025 - I hope they don’t increase the pricing) for the value. If you’re considering whether this is for you, I highly encourage you to take the jump. This has hands-down been the most helpful device and app I have ever used for my chronic illnesses and disability management.

reviews.title: Such a good start
reviews.text: I have long covid/chronic fatigue syndrome, and this has been such a game changer for getting some actual objective data to help me figure things out. Unless you have a really good doctor or support system, it can feel like a complete guessing game to figure out how I’m doing and what’s working. This has been so helpful as an all in one tracker for heart data and notes and symptoms, and the morning score can be a really useful guide for planning your day. It’s so much more affordable than most medical things in the US. At full price it’s $100 for the device and $20 a month at time of writing, but that is an investment that’s paid off dividends for me. I’m finally making progress in my recovery.

reviews.title: 12 months in (8 months with membership)
reviews.text:
The app is helpful, but the support is NEXT LEVEL. Visible has a team of folks — actual humans— that have responded and coached me through any time I’ve needed help. It’s no surprise that many of the folks who use this app *do* need help customizing it for our weirdo bodies. 
I found the app (without the paid membership) really helpful. But when i was able (and not all people are) to add on the sensor and membership, I did it immediately. No regrets. 
Also, when i had to pause my membership, it was no problem. When I resumed it, I was pleasantly surprised with all the new features and support. The excellent user group even got me back on Facebook!

reviews.title: Helping invisible illnesses heal
reviews.text: I really appreciate a company specifically working towards healing the symptoms of invisible illnesses. these illnesses are often complicated and confusing, and the data and suggestions from Visible make every day progress on my health journey. i’m looking forward to seeing more improvements from the brand, such as additional app, improvements and wearable technology charging improvements.

reviews.title: Even better than expected
reviews.text: I am so, so grateful for this app. It’s very easy to use and gives me important insights on when I need to rest. I’m horrible at resting when I need to. The app gives me a tangible way to easily track my body’s needs. It serves as a reminder to listen to my cues. It’s very easy to use and I don’t run into crazy glitches. I really can’t say enough good about this app. As someone with ME/CFS, POTS, and Loeys-Dietz Syndrome, my cardiac health and energy conservation is so important. Thanks for helping me feel visible.

reviews.title: Great!
reviews.text: Used this for a year, sometimes everyday for months at a time or sometimes on and off, and received AMAZING information on what activities are harder to do for me and how my energy and capacity can fluctuate from one month to another. For example, I always ‘felt’ that showers were tiring but I didn’t realize how physically exhausting they were until this app. Now I can count that as part of my spoons for the day rather than crashing out more consistently. Also a great app to log symptoms, meds/supplements, movement, and so much more all in just one. It’s really amazing and the first of its kind with all of the elements it brings together. Would recommend to anyone in a heartbeat.

reviews.title: Delightful Friend Who Counts Your Daily Spoons
reviews.text: Thank you, Crumb, you know who you are, for recommending this delightfully sassy and perfectly helpful app. I’ve never before been so enlightened and infuriated to be told I’m reaching the end of my spoon limit for the day. To have a friend that counts your spoons for you is a delightful thing. Thank you for telling me to try this armband plus tracker. I find myself working out differently when the “exertion” timer is enabled, and while it makes me grumpy to be told that I ought to slow down — I really do need to slow down. Thank you so much for helping me live a steadier life.

reviews.title: OG Long Covid Thriver!
reviews.text: I love this app! I primarily use it to keep an eye on pacing through the day and the week overall. It allows me to watch an app that tracks me automatically and warns me of possible crashes instead of an app that pushes me (fitness apps) or requires me to enter info manually (so many other chronic illnesses apps). I could do more, like evening check-ins, to get more info out but I try to put my focus and energy into the good and joy of what I can do and try not to focus too much on my symptoms so I am not great about using the self reporting tools. They are there though and quite useful during crashes or infections. Most importantly for me, I can see where I am at with my “spoons” for the day and know if I should slow down a bit if I’m doing too much. It’s helped me to level out to have less crashes and more good days, more somewhat productive days! It is $20/mo which can be limiting while on disability but I have found the cost worth it for me considering what I get. And the support is incredible. Extremely grateful this group of researchers build such a needed and useful app!!

reviews.title: Not accessible
reviews.text:
For an app made for the disabled, this is INCREDIBLY expensive. Not accessible to the people that actually need it.

The free version is also not helpful. The stability score compares everything to your “baseline” but if you’re in a chronic crash with terrible symptoms and terrible sleep then it gives you a good stability score because you’re close to your “baseline.” Like no, I’m not stable and being horrible all the time isn’t a baseline. If I put my sleep is awful and symptoms are awful then it says I’m good because it’s my baseline.

reviews.title: Pacing and a sense of control
reviews.text: Dealing w long covid, you can feel crazy, alone, and helpless to understand what’s going on with your body and how to help yourself. This easy to use wearable with app is incredibly helpful to give a sense of continuity, peace, and control by tracking what’s happening with your body and giving you info to slow down before you push yourself too much. The creator really knows what’s needed as he too suffers from an energy disorder. Great, helpful app from kind, helpful people.

reviews.title: visible
reviews.text: i have pots and gastroparesis. this has been such an amazing way to understand my body better. especially during crashes. great way to help me pace myself and shows my doctors how much my heart rate fluctuates.

reviews.title: It has really helped with my pacing
reviews.text: I don’t have great body awareness. I often push myself when I should be relaxing. When I overdo it sometimes it takes days for me to recover. If I’m pacing myself correctly recovery time is way less, hours instead of days

reviews.title: Lead me out of burnout
reviews.text: Ever have that friend who always tells you the truth and it's both really annoying and exceptionally helpful? That's visible. It showed me how often I over exerted myself and taught me how to reserve some energy for later. I was actually able to build a reserve so I could push through on days when I had to without burning out. This has made my life so much better.

reviews.title: Visible Changed Everything
reviews.text: I LOVE Visible for helping with my chronic illnesses! I use the pacing function most often, but I also am so happy it alerts me when my heart rate is high so I can calm it down. Additionally, I’ve used the data it creates to show my doctor that my symptoms aren’t “all in my head” as I’ve heard too many times before. Overall I highly recommend it!

reviews.title: If you’re Chronically Ill, this is it
reviews.text:
The team that has made this is amazing. The founder sends updates about what they’re working on and they support research using information volunteered from users (don’t worry, this is only the case if you opt in, they don’t just steal data). 
Visible has made a huge difference in knowing what adjustments I need to make each day. I have a dynamic disability and Visible takes the guess work out of it. Love it!

reviews.title: Very happy so far
reviews.text: I received my armband 2 weeks ago and it’s been great. I was already using just the app to track symptoms and take my morning hr, but the addition of the armband has made the data more robust with the ability to see my hrv in real time.

reviews.title: Helpful Insights
reviews.text: I’ve been using Visible for a shorting but have already begun seeing things I had not before. I can say it is already slowing me down which is good, I’m truly hoping to learn to feel, see and live better each day. Because this is the beginning to a better healthier me!

reviews.title: Nothing like it
reviews.text: This app has changed my life and how I mange my illness. Never before have I had a tool this important and easy to use in managing my chronic illness. From the little lessons to the morning check ins everything is simple and effective. I cannot recommend this enough!! Even if you don’t get the armband and just do symptom tracking and morning check ins it is well worth your time!!

reviews.title: Really helpful
reviews.text: I was searching for a health tracker that could help me manage my energy because I have a tendency to go past my limits then crash. When I came across Visible I was intrigued because it’s designed for someone who’s dealing with a chronic illness, which is so different than other trackers. So, far it’s helping me understand how much energy I have, how much energy tasks take, and it’s helping me shift my mindset around what I “should” be able to do. I wish I’d had this throughout dealing with the illness I deal with.

reviews.title: Definitely worth the cost
reviews.text: This app/tracker is great. The armband is very comfortable.  The tracking is great, I am able to track physical and mental health and provide actual data to my providers. When I was tracking on my own it was difficult to keep a journal and pull that information together for providers. Also, when they can see the heart rate variability and the symptoms visuals they can’t just dismiss it like they have been doing.

reviews.title: Lowest Stress Chronic Illness Tracker
reviews.text: Whoever designed this app clearly had the end users in mind. This app requires very little input from the user. Two, 1-minute check-ins in the morning and at night quickly became part of my routine. It feels cathartic to reflect on my symptoms every night, and the HRV readings in the mornings have been great daily predictors of the likelihood that my symptoms will get triggered later on.

reviews.title: From free user to paid subscriber
reviews.text:
i started using the free version of the visible app a little over a year ago to help find patterns in my activity that were leading to bed-bound crashes. 

after tracking my symptoms for about 9 months and seeing some improvement, i decided to becone a paid subscriber. 
my doctor appreciates the more detailed data, i am able to pace much more efficiently, and i've seen even more improvements. my hrv has increased by an average of 10 points and my daily stability scores are consistently higher. 

i do believe that using this app, in conjunction with finally finding a doctor who will read published data & has allowed me to start off-label medication, has led to me gaining more functional capacity than i've had for almost a decade. i also feel good about the studies my data is being used in, so that others, including my children who have likely inherited some of these traits, will not suffer the way so many of us have. 

:: for reference, i have been diagnosed with the following. i live with debilitating chronic pain & fatigue. it was likely brought on from a viral illness in 2014. 

AuDHD
ME/CFS 
POTS
Fibromyalgia
MCAS
H-EDS
Endometriosis, Adenomyosis, & Fibroids
Diffuse Autonomic Neuropathy
CPTSD

reviews.title: Amazing for those with  autoimmune diseases
reviews.text: I have RA, and before I found Visible, I was constantly crashing and flaring. I am a former athlete and high-energy person. I come from a long line of women who work tirelessly in all areas of their lives. When I was diagnosed with RA, I couldn’t figure out what my exertion levels really should be. My old ways of exercising and moving through life weren’t working anymore. I found myself unable to do what I used to and unknowingly doing too much to the point of being bedridden for days after over doing it. Using Visible has drastically changed my quality of life, because I now understand how to work within my own unique energy levels without overdoing it. I’m able to be active and prioritize where I put my energy every day. Since starting to use visible 6 months ago, I’ve only crashed one time. And I was able to recover from it more quickly than I used to. Overall,  I can now almost completely avoid crashing thanks to Visible!

reviews.title: Good app
reviews.text: I’ve been using the Visible app for a while now and I find it to be beneficial in learning how to pace. When I’m consistent in completing the check ins, i can share this information with my drs and they have a better idea of how I’ve been doing. This information helps me to understand my own progress and those using this information to further research, with your permission of course.

reviews.title: Unfortunate issue
